title: Software Development Engineer, Building Connectivity Engineering
description:
Every Amazon data center runs on networks no customer ever sees: the corporate network that engineers and tools use to reach the fleet, the segmented networks that cameras and badge readers ride on, the network for building systems, and the isolated controls networks behind power and cooling. Building Connectivity Engineering (BCE), part of AWS Networking, owns the design and operation of those fabrics in every Amazon data center, and builds them into more than 100 new sites a year. Building Connectivity Software Systems (BCSS) is the software team inside BCE.
We build the controller for these networks. It holds the intended state of every fabric as a model, computes everything a new site needs (addresses, routing identifiers, ports, cabling, device registration) before a technician plugs in the first rack, renders device configuration from the model, and drives the deployment and monitoring platforms that AWS Networking already runs. The first production release went live in September 2026 and took a site build that used to need about twenty hand-run steps down to one request. Most of the controller is still ahead of us.
We are hiring Software Development Engineers to build the next releases: a versioned model of intended network state with full history and rollback, device configuration rendered from that model instead of written by hand, and the orchestration that takes a site from a plan to live traffic with one physical touch. You will design services, write the design documents for them, build them on AWS, prove them in shadow mode against real sites, and run them in production. The network engineers who hold the fabric knowledge are your partners; your code is the engine their models run on.
Key job responsibilities
* Design and build services in AWS (Lambda, Step Functions, DynamoDB, EventBridge, CDK), modeled with Smithy and deployed through pipelines you own.
* Write the design document for what you build. Every engineer on this team writes designs; it is a core part of the job, and seniority is not the gate.
* Integrate with the systems of record in AWS Networking (IP address management, device registry, routing-policy store, configuration store and release, deployment, cabling plans), and find out what each contract actually does, against the real service, before committing to a date.
* Prove correctness in shadow mode: compute what the automation would do for a site, diff it against what engineers did by hand, and get to zero discrepancies before any cutover.
* Own what you ship in production: metrics, alarms, runbooks, and a turn in the team's on-call rotation, which covers the new services and the ones the team inherited.
* Keep fabric knowledge out of the code. New fabrics, site types and rack types arrive as models the network engineers author; your job is to make the second one cost a configuration change.
* Estimate honestly: size work by how novel it is and how many systems outside the team it touches, raise partner asks early, and say what is unknown.
A day in the life
You pick up a card to add a new reservation type to the allocation service. Before writing code you spend an hour against the real partner API in a test account and find that the contract does not do what its wiki page says, so you write that down, re-size the card, and raise the ask with the partner team that morning instead of three weeks in. The afternoon is a design review of a teammate's state machine change, where the question you keep asking is what happens on the retry, and your own code review landing with its shadow-mode diff attached. A few times a year you are the on-call engineer for a week, and the team expects that week to be your work.
About the team
BCSS, formed in May 2026. We bring software engineering practice to a problem space that has not had software developers, and we never cut corners: slow is smooth, and smooth is fast. Our stance in one line is a team tenet: we don't just make a change, we make a changer. Our software runs on AWS and operates entirely detached from production data traffic.
We work inside an operating model where network fabric teams run like software teams: they own their business logic, expose APIs, and measure outcomes. BCSS builds the software; every fabric team owns its automation roadmap and its adoption. Design reviews are open and argued; the best objection in the room wins, whoever raised it.

Building Connectivity Engineering (BCE), part of AWS Networking, owns the design and operation of those fabrics in every Amazon data center, and builds them into more than 100 new sites a year. Building Connectivity Software Systems (BCSS) is the software team inside BCE.
We build the controller for these networks. It holds the intended state of every fabric as a model, computes everything a new site needs (addresses, routing identifiers, ports, cabling, device registration) before a technician plugs in the first rack, renders device configuration from the model, and drives the deployment and monitoring platforms that AWS Networking already runs. The first production release went live in September 2026 and took a site build that used to need about twenty hand-run steps down to one request. Most of the controller is still ahead of us.
We are hiring Software Development Engineers to build the next releases: a versioned model of intended network state with full history and rollback, device configuration rendered from that model instead of written by hand, and the orchestration that takes a site from a plan to live traffic with one physical touch. You will design services, write the design documents for them, build them on AWS, prove them in shadow mode against real sites, and run them in production. The network engineers who hold the fabric knowledge are your partners; your code is the engine their models run on.
Key job responsibilities
* Design and build services in AWS (Lambda, Step Functions, DynamoDB, EventBridge, CDK), modeled with Smithy and deployed through pipelines you own.
* Write the design document for what you build. Every engineer on this team writes designs; it is a core part of the job, and seniority is not the gate.
* Integrate with the systems of record in AWS Networking (IP address management, device registry, routing-policy store, configuration store and release, deployment, cabling plans), and find out what each contract actually does, against the real service, before committing to a date.
* Prove correctness in shadow mode: compute what the automation would do for a site, diff it against what engineers did by hand, and get to zero discrepancies before any cutover.
* Own what you ship in production: metrics, alarms, runbooks, and a turn in the team's on-call rotation, which covers the new services and the ones the team inherited.
* Keep fabric knowledge out of the code. New fabrics, site types and rack types arrive as models the network engineers author; your job is to make the second one cost a configuration change.
* Estimate honestly: size work by how novel it is and how many systems outside the team it touches, raise partner asks early, and say what is unknown.
A day in the life
You pick up a card to add a new reservation type to the allocation service. Before writing code you spend an hour against the real partner API in a test account and find that the contract does not do what its wiki page says, so you write that down, re-size the card, and raise the ask with the partner team that morning instead of three weeks in. The afternoon is a design review of a teammate's state machine change, where the question you keep asking is what happens on the retry, and your own code review landing with its shadow-mode diff attached. A few times a year you are the on-call engineer for a week, and the team expects that week to be your work.
About the team
BCSS, formed in May 2026. We bring software engineering practice to a problem space that has not had software developers, and we never cut corners: slow is smooth, and smooth is fast. Our stance in one line is a team tenet: we don't just make a change, we make a changer. Our software runs on AWS and operates entirely detached from production data traffic.
We work inside an operating model where network fabric teams run like software teams: they own their business logic, expose APIs, and measure outcomes. BCSS builds the software; every fabric team owns its automation roadmap and its adoption. Design reviews are open and argued; the best objection in the room wins, whoever raised it.

title: Software Development Manager, EBS Server Agility
description:
If leading a team that builds secure, autonomous systems to test, deploy, and patch server software for one of the world's largest storage services excites you, the EBS Server Agility team is the place to do it. EBS is a foundational AWS service on which most other AWS services depend, and our teams build and operate the Continuous Integration platform and the deployment and patching infrastructure that keep EBS server software fast to ship, current, and secure across 400,000 bare-metal servers, infrastructure that serves millions of AWS customers and exabytes of data every day.
We are looking for a Software Development Manager to lead an engineering team in our DevOps space. This is the space that spans Continuous Integration, which builds the platform that decides whether a change is safe to ship, and Deployments and Patching, which safely rolls that change out to a stateful storage engine serving live customer I/O. Both sit in the critical path for feature velocity and security compliance, and both are places where strong engineering leadership has outsized impact.
You will not be writing the code or designing the systems yourself. You will lead the engineers who do: hiring and growing the team, setting clear technical direction, removing ambiguity, and delivering results predictably. You will decide where your systems sit in their lifecycle, define goals tied to business needs, and build the mechanisms that let the team deliver consistently without wearing out its best people. The guiding philosophy is simple and demanding: every manual step in the operator path is a defect in the system, and your team builds the test frameworks, CI infrastructure, and deployment services that engineer that toil away.
Server CI and deployment at EBS shape how the software evolves to support new hardware platforms, new partitions (including edge and Outpost), and new operational models. You will partner with principal engineers and leaders across EC2 and EBS, and represent your team's work in discussions that shape how EBS evolves. If you want your leadership to have real impact at AWS scale, and you are excited by building a team that builds systems that test, deploy, and patch themselves, we would love to talk to you.
Key job responsibilities
- Lead, hire, develop, and promote a team of software engineers (up to Senior SDE, L6) across the CI and Deployments domains, building a team with sustainable on-call and clear growth paths
- Own and set the technical direction and roadmap across both the CI platform and the deployment and patching systems, and be accountable for how they work together
- Deliver a CI platform that answers "is this change safe to deploy to 400,000 servers," including distributed test orchestration, intelligent test selection, and observability across x86 and Graviton
- Deliver deployment pipelines and automated security patching that safely update a stateful storage engine across all AWS regions and partitions with zero customer impact and manifest consistency on a biweekly cadence
- Drive toward secure, autonomous operations: automated canary analysis, rollback, anomaly detection, and self-healing automation that takes the operator out of the loop
- Own operational health across both domains: on-call, patch compliance, and the cadences that keep the fleet green
- Define goals tied to business needs and deliver them predictably, building mechanisms so the team ships consistently
- Lead the team through change with clarity and empathy, and influence technical direction beyond your immediate team
A day in the life
Your day moves across many disparate topics. You might align the team on a roadmap for the quarter, coach an engineer through a design, review progress against goals, and make a principled call that trades a little speed for safety on a change headed to the fleet. You will remove blockers, set priorities, and keep on-call sustainable while the team ships. You will partner with principal engineers and leaders across EBS and EC2, and you will represent your team's work to senior leadership.
This is a high-visibility role. The work in this space affects every EBS customer, and your team's output is regularly reviewed by senior leadership. You will collaborate across organizational boundaries, influence technical direction beyond your immediate team, and build a team that is better for your presence but does not need you to be successful.
We value managers who lead through ambiguity, reduce toil through smart automation, make principled tradeoffs between speed and safety, hire and grow strong engineers, and elevate everyone around them.
About the team
EBS Server Agility is the DevOps space for EBS Server, owning the Continuous Integration platform and the server deployment and patching infrastructure. Our engineers build distributed test orchestration and qualification systems, deployment pipelines that safely deliver validated server software to 400,000 bare-metal servers, automated patching that keeps software secure on a biweekly cadence, metrics and crash observability, and secure operational tooling for autonomous operations. We move fast to deliver for customers while maintaining operational excellence across these mission-critical services.
We are a Boston-based group building toward a future where server software tests, patches, and deploys itself: safely, securely, on schedule, with full visibility. There is significant greenfield opportunity, because CI and safe deployment for stateful bare-metal systems at global scale have almost no off-the-shelf solutions, so our teams design from first principles.
We are dedicated to supporting the people on the team. We have a broad mix of experience levels and tenures, and we are building an environment that celebrates knowledge-sharing and mentorship. Senior members give one-on-one mentoring and thorough, but kind, design and code reviews. We care about career growth and work to assign projects that stretch each engineer so they feel empowered to take on more complex problems over time.

title: Software Engineer II - AI/ML, Neuron Inference, Inference

The Annapurna Labs team at Amazon Web Services (AWS) builds the AWS Neuron SDK, the software development kit used to accelerate deep learning and GenAI workloads on AWS Trainium machine learning accelerators.
The Neuron Inference organization is at the forefront of optimizing inference performance for a wide range of ML models and model architectures on AWS's custom ML accelerators. We combine deep hardware knowledge with ML expertise to push the boundaries of what's
possible in AI acceleration.
As part of the broader Neuron organization, our team works across multiple technology layers — from frameworks and kernels through to compiler, runtime, and collectives. We not only optimize performance on open weight models but also contribute to future architecture designs and work closely with customers to enable optimal performance on their models. This role offers a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of machine learning, high-performance computing, and distributed architectures, where you'll help shape the future of AI acceleration technology.
As a Software Engineer II - AI/ML, you will design and implement business-critical features and own the performance of models on AWS Trainium end to end. We operate in spaces that are very large, yet our teams remain small and agile. There is no blueprint. We're inventing. We're experimenting. It is a very unique learning culture. The team works closely with customers on their model enablement, providing direct support and optimization expertise to ensure their machine learning workloads achieve optimal performance on AWS ML accelerators. The team also collaborates with open source ecosystems to provide seamless integration and bring peak performance at scale for customers and developers.
This role is responsible for development, enablement, and performance tuning of a wide variety of LLM model families, including massive-scale large language models like the GLM, GPT-OSS, Kimi, and beyond. The Model Enablement team works side by side with compiler engineers and runtime engineers to create, build, and tune distributed inference solutions with AWS Trainium.

title: Sr Customer Solutions Manager, Strategic Accounts
description:
We are seeking a Sr. Customer Solutions Manager (CSM) to join our Strategic Accounts organization. In this new, highly visible role, you will be responsible for helping guide AWS customers along their multi-year journey to the cloud, ensuring that all AWS teams are working together effectively and efficiently to deliver outcomes for the customer.
Our team is committed to helping large industry-leading enterprise customers enable their digital transformation journeys. Our primary goal is to meet customers where they are in their cloud journey and work backwards from their industry specific needs to transform their business and their entire industry. Our team speaks the language of our customers, which means that we focus on business outcomes on behalf of our customers, whether that is how we build products and solutions, how we sell, how we deliver, or how we partner.
If you are excited about the prospect of using your cloud architecture experience to assist our most valuable customers, tackling challenging problems, have a hand in shaping the future of agentic AI and cloud adoption, enhancing and growing your own skills, and having fun, then we would love to hear from you.
You will be a critical partner to our customers, leveraging your experience with large scale agentic AI and cloud transformations and helping shepherd them through their stages of AWS adoption. Guiding the customer through the operational, educational, and governance aspects of a successful AWS cloud journey.
You will interface with customer and AWS leadership, driving collaboration between the other core account groups (Sales, Support, Solutions Architecture, and Professional Services), product/engineering teams, and customer teams, planning and supporting major workload migrations and modernizations. You will translate strategic initiatives in the account plan into executable actions, working backwards from our customers key milestones. You will manage cadence by leading the reporting and tracking functions along the way. The execution of education plans, roadmap to business outcome alignments, Executive Briefing Sessions, and technical customer engagements are a few items owned by the CSM that are critical to the success of our customer’s cloud journey.
You are encouraged to think big, invent and take ownership on customer challenges. You will not only bring the best of AWS/Amazon to our customers, you will proactively help solve the customer’s challenges through new ideas, tools and mechanisms.
Successful candidates will have a strong technical background, familiar with agentic AI/GenAI, be aware of details that matter, have excellent problem-solving abilities, and be exemplary communicators both at the executive and project team level. You will be a peer leader, have the ability to gain stakeholder buy-in, negotiate and lead virtual teams. Your enterprise cloud experience and operational excellence will influence the team’s decisions, provide insight, and help drive secure and robust solutions.
You will evangelize AWS services and influence customers for adopting them. You should be passionate about delivering a great customer experience by deploying AWS solutions and driving innovation, and also be obsessed with contributing to the day-to-day management of customers’ successful adoption of AWS.
Key job responsibilities
You will establish a deep understanding of your customer’s business vision, culture and processes, and evangelize AWS services and influence customers to adopt the right solution at the right time. Customer Solutions Managers (CSM) are responsible for four focus areas:
1/Accelerating AWS Adoption through Delivery and Execution
2/Identify & Align on Strategic Opportunities: CSMs work with the Account team to work backwards from the customer to identify and pursue strategic cloud opportunities. These strategic cloud opportunities can include but are not limited to large-scale workload migrations & modernizations, GenAI/Agentic, data and analytics, digital innovation, high performance computing, product innovation, and business agility.
3/Customer Enablement, you will serve as the customer’s cloud journey coach and be the voice of the customer within AWS, evangelizing customer needs to AWS leadership, product, and engineering teams.
4/Implement governance structures to effectively govern both our partnership with the customer, and the customer’s adoption of AWS.
These interconnected focus areas will enable CSMs to effectively drive customer cloud adoption, pursue strategic growth opportunities, and empower customer success - all of which are critical to achieving AWS’s business objectives. By aligning CSM activities, goals, and opportunities under these focus areas, CSMs ensure a disciplined, customer-centric approach that maximizes business impact and revenue realization for AWS.

title: Sr. Product Designer, AWS Billing
description:
Every AWS customer, from a solo developer to a Fortune 100 finance team, eventually asks the same questions. What am I spending? Why am I spending it? What should I do about it? AWS Billing answers those questions for millions of customers, inside a business running at a $169 billion annualized revenue run rate.
That job is changing as AI agents are starting to act on customers' behalf. They forecast spend, recommend commitments, flag anomalies, and increasingly take action on customer’s behalf. When an agent touches someone's money, the design questions get harder: What is it allowed to do on its own? How does it explain itself? How does the customer stay in control and undo what it did? Few products anywhere face these questions at this scale or with these stakes.
We're looking for a Senior Product Designer to help answer them. You'll define how customers and AI agents work together to understand, forecast, and control cloud spend, and you'll set the patterns other teams build on.
- Design for trust where it matters most. Billing is where customers decide whether to trust AWS with their money, and where AI has to earn that trust.
- Define agentic UX, not just screens. Shape what agents do on a customer's behalf, where humans approve, and how automated actions stay transparent and reversible.
- Work with a wide range of customers and rich data. Design for developers, FinOps practitioners, CFOs, and channel partners, using some of the richest usage and spend data at AWS.
- Ship as an embedded partner. Work alongside product, engineering, and data science from problem framing through post-launch iteration.
Key job responsibilities
- Frame ambiguous problems before solving them. Drive clarity when requirements, customers, and feasibility are undefined.
- Define how AI agents act on customers' behalf: what they do autonomously, where humans approve, and how customers take control back.
- Design trust patterns that surface an agent's confidence, reasoning, and attribution, so customers understand why it acts.
- Design human-in-the-loop, approval, and undo patterns for actions that move money.
- Create coherent experiences across conversational, agent-driven, and console interfaces.
- Lead design from problem framing through launch, then use data signals to improve what ships.
- Partner early with data science, legal, and policy as co-designers on AI features with financial or compliance complexity.
- Establish patterns and standards that become how the team operates. Mentor other designers.
- Write narratives and strategy documents that move decisions forward, and present them to senior leadership.
A day in the life
Your morning starts with usage data from an anomaly-alert flow you shipped last month. Then you meet your PM and engineering lead to frame a new problem: when should an agent pause spend without asking? You prototype two directions with AI tools and bring them to critique. After lunch, you work with data science and legal on how an agent explains a commitment recommendation. You end the day refining a narrative for leadership review. Your customers range from solo builders to CFOs. Your work decides whether they trust an agent with their money.
About the team
AWS Billing sits at the intersection of trust and scale. Every customer, from a first-time builder to a Fortune 100 enterprise, relies on us to make spending transparent and controllable. We are a tight-knit design group within the larger AWS Design organization. We work with product, engineering, and data science. We move fast without lowering the craft bar. We are designing agents that can spot a cost spike and help stop it before the bill arrives. We believe billing should not just work. It should build confidence. title: Sr. Product Manager, NAS Ship Cost Optimization
description:
At Amazon, we're working to be the Earth’s most customer-centric company. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people. This Product managers will be responsible for driving optimization efforts across various organizations and processes to improve shipping costs at Amazon. This includes defining the right set of metrics and processes, establishing ambitious goals and driving towards them, working with technology and operations partners to design, develop and deploy intelligent processes and improvements.
The North American Stores (NAS) organization is focused on continuously optimizing its P&L to drive long-term profitability. One of the most significant levers? Outbound fulfillment costs. The NAS Ship Cost Optimization (SCO) team tackles this head-on—leveraging technology for scale and launching innovative products that optimize costs systematically and with measurable impact.
This team has delivered over $1 billion+ in cumulative bottom-line improvements over the past four years by reducing packaging waste, correcting dimensional defects, optimizing regional fulfillment, and building Gen-AI products that reimagine how Amazon collaborates with selling partners. In 2026, the team is targeting significant savings through initiatives spanning cube reduction, AI-powered vendor outreach, regionalization strategies, sortability defect reduction, and improved placement—against a total addressable opportunity of $1.5B+.
As a Sr Product Manager on this team, you will own products and initiatives that directly improve the profitability of one of Amazon's largest businesses. You will develop a deep understanding of the inputs driving ship costs—placement, regional fulfillment, sortability, ship method choices, and dimensions—and translate that knowledge into products, policies, and partnerships that deliver hundreds of millions in savings. You will work across partner teams spanning Supply Chain Technology, Operations, Transportation, Finance, and Category Management, and you will leverage AI and automation to build the next generation of cost optimization products.
This is a role for someone who thinks in systems, communicates with precision, and thrives at the intersection of data, product strategy, and cross-organizational influence.

Represent the team in leadership forums, crafting data-driven narratives that communicate progress, risks, and trade-offs to senior leaders with clarity and confidence.

You start the morning reviewing product metrics and triaging customer feedback to decide where to focus. You close the day by updating your team on progress and aligning on next steps.

The NAS Ship Cost Optimization team is a small, high-impact product team that punches well above its weight. Over the past four years, the team has delivered $1B+ in cumulative bottom-line improvements to the Stores P&L by building innovative products—including the Gen-AI powered CRISP service—and championing cost-smart policies across the fulfillment network.

title: Sr. Site Technical Manager, Devices Postponement Operations (DPO)
description:
The Senior Site Technical Manager (STM) is responsible for development, qualification, and validation of assembly, test, and pack out processes for Amazon’s Devices Products in a multi-product, automation-focused factory. STMs troubleshoot and resolve technical, material, and process issues, oversee assembly and packout processes, drive cost, process, and yield improvements. STMs apply lean methodologies, support site acceptance testing (SAT), and DFx (Design for Automation, Manufacturing, Cost). STMs work closely with Amazon’s Contract Manufacturer (CM) and Amazon’s product design and automation engineers.
Key job responsibilities
As Senior STM, you:
• own resolution of technical issues for multiple products in a fast-paced, automation-focused factory;
• work quickly and collaboratively with colleagues and suppliers to identify, troubleshoot, and resolve automation, material, process, and procedure issues;
• drive continuous improvements to manufacturing and automation processes, including oversight of the Contract Manufacturer’s continuous improvement program;
• identify and design required assembly and test fixtures for new and existing products;
• work with others on new product design-for-automation, create standard operating procedures and processes, and oversee the Contract Manufacturer’s operator training program to ensure readiness before production;
• identify and drive quality improvement and cost reduction goals, including oversight of the Contract Manufacturer’s incoming quality control processes;
• oversee the Contract Manufacturer’s preventive maintenance program to ensure equipment availability meets production requirements.
A day in the life
The STM will be actively engaged in managing the factory and its processes, on the floor working with suppliers and operators, monitoring the performance of packout lines, and identifying ideas for continuous improvement. As new programs are introduced to the site, the STM will play a key role in identifying the manufacturing processes to aid in scoping work and cost. And as issues arise, the STM will be the key leader to bring together all the technical resources needed to quickly diagnose, triage, contain, fix, and restore services to enable the site to meet its on-time delivery goals.
About the team
Device Postponement Operations (DPO) is Amazon Lab126’s team responsible for in-region postponement, customization, and pack-out of Amazon’s innovative devices. We finalize the assembly of devices using automated assembly and pack-out lines so that Amazon can customize products to meet just-in-time demand. We enable Amazon to deliver very quickly to our customers the right configuration of a product at low cost and high quality.
Amazon’s Lab126 began in 2004 as a subsidiary of Amazon.com, Inc., originally creating the best-selling Kindle family of products. Lab126 have produced great devices like Fire TV, the Echo Family of products, and Astro. We deliver delightfully unique Amazon experiences, giving customers instant access to everything, digital, or physical.

- Experience with process improvements (Lean Six Sigma and/or Kaizen)
- Bachelor of Science in Mechatronics, Mechanical Engineering, or equivalent

- Experience developing functional specifications, design verification plans, and functional test procedures while launching programs in a phase-gate release (e.g., xVT, Ramp) and acceptance-test process (FAT, SAT); basic GD&T and DFx (Manufacturing, Cost, Test)
- Demonstrated knowledge and experience with quality concepts, tools, and methods such as 8D, DOE, APQP, PPAP, FMEA, Measurement Systems Analysis, fishbone diagrams, 5Whys
- Data management and analysis using Minitab; Yield reporting with Pareto, Cp/Cpk, GR&R
- Experience with precision measurement and inspection devices such as calipers, micrometers, height gages, OMM, profilometers, optical inspection devices, multi-meters, and torque wrenches
- Manufacturing knowledge and relevant work experience in Supplier Quality, Product Quality, or Product Reliability
- Demonstrated ability to resolve complex issues in creative, efficient, and effective ways, including handling ambiguous or undefined challenges
- Demonstrated ability to gain deep understanding of the business and end user needs quickly, using customer insights and data
- 10+ years' experience in operations, working with and managing OEM/CM suppliers, throughout the product life cycle from Concept to EOL with minimum 5 years experience as STM
Preferred qualifications: - Master's degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or equivalent
- Master's degree in Industrial, Mechanical, Mechatronics, or Electrical Engineering, or equivalent

- Experience working with interdisciplinary teams to execute product design from concept to production
- Experience with the project management of technical projects

description:
We are seeking a candidate with a passion for e-commerce and a desire to make a real impact on global customers in a Day One business. Our mission is to expand selection from US-based retailers and brand owners worldwide. Although we are already a multi-billion-dollar business, we believe we are just getting started, as less than 5% of US-based sellers have started their international journey. This role offers the opportunity to innovate and elevate the seller and customer experience on a global scale.
As a Strategic Account Manager on the Amazon Global Selling team, you will work with top Amazon.com sellers, helping them expand their online retail business to Amazon's stores worldwide. You will work with sellers leadership teams, identifying key decision-makers and aligning them to prioritize actions required to expand their online retail business to Amazon's global stores such as Amazon.co.uk, Amazon.de, Amazon.com.mx. • Prepare and conduct monthly business reviews with CXO stakeholders in sellers' organizations regarding progress and strategies to increase their revenue on Amazon's global websites.
• Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders and program leaders to drive business growth.

The Amazon Global Selling team's vision is to be the first choice for all US retail businesses to go global. We operate with the agility of a startup and a singular mission to empower US-based sellers to expand their businesses worldwide. We are committed to building an AI-native, agentic organization — one where AI agents increasingly handle execution at breadth and speed, while our account management team owns the strategy, the deep insights, the judgment, and the outcomes. title: Test Lab Manager
description:
Amazon is building the next generation of multi-purpose robotics systems, and scaling from prototype to production. We are looking for an experienced Test Lab Manager to play a key leadership role in proving robots are ready for deployment. This is a chance to join a growing System Verification and Validation team at a pivotal moment and build a lab organization from the ground up. You will own the processes that keep our hardware and physical system test environments running, and you will directly shape how we verify and validate the next generation of Amazon robotics.
As a Test Lab Manager, you will lead a multidisciplinary team of infrastructure, operations, and maintenance staff spanning multiple lab locations that support hardware and physical system testing. Your team runs tests and experiments, operates and maintains test fixtures, lab equipment, control systems, and motion capture systems, coordinates test intake and scheduling, and keeps test uptime high through proactive and corrective maintenance. You will be responsible for standing up new lab spaces, establishing the processes and systems that manage incoming test demand, and growing and developing the team as the lab footprint expands. If you are energized by leading hands-on technical teams, building operational excellence into a scaling organization, and enabling robotics verification and validation, we want to hear from you.
Key job responsibilities
- Lead execution of hardware and physical system test and experimentation campaigns across multiple lab locations, ensuring tests are run safely, on schedule, and with high-quality data in support of verification and validation goals.
- Partner with cross-functional project groups—hardware, software, systems, and quality engineering teams—to understand test requirements, plan lab capacity, and support experimentation from setup through data collection and review.
- Build and own test request intake and management processes and systems, standardizing how test demand is submitted, prioritized, scheduled, and tracked across sites.
- Provide visibility into lab testing activities, capacity, and equipment availability by developing dashboards and reporting that help stakeholders track test status, utilization, and throughput across sites.
- Lead and develop a multidisciplinary lab team (infrastructure, controls, operations, and maintenance staff) across multiple test lab locations, providing coverage across shifts and on-call rotations.
- Own the operation, availability, and uptime of test environments, fixtures, lab equipment, control systems (PLC, I/O), motion capture systems, and environmental test chambers.
- Establish and continuously improve lab operational processes, SOPs, and documentation to enable safe, repeatable, and high-throughput testing.
- Oversee preventive and corrective maintenance programs for lab equipment and electro-mechanical systems to maximize test readiness.
- Stand up new lab spaces, coordinating equipment sourcing, installation, calibration, and onboarding of staff to bring labs online on schedule.
- Ensure safety compliance and manage lab safety protocols specific to robotics hardware testing (e.g., gantry interlocks, robot safety devices, lockout procedures).
A day in the life
You might start your morning reviewing the test request queue and the day's schedule across your lab sites, reallocating staff to keep high-priority verification campaigns on track. You could spend part of the day running a hardware test campaign alongside a cross-functional project team, then work with your controls engineers to resolve an issue with an automated test cell. In the afternoon you might refine your test intake process based on feedback from engineering partners, review a dashboard of lab utilization to rebalance capacity, and coach a team member stepping into a new area of ownership. Throughout, you will remove bottlenecks, improve processes, and keep your labs running safely and reliably.
About the team
We are a growing System Verification and Validation organization building the lab infrastructure that validates robotic hardware and physical systems across multiple dimensions of performance and reliability as we scale from prototype to production. This Test Lab Manager role will lead the first dedicated lab engineering organization on the team, spanning multiple sites and disciplines. If you want to help build a lab organization from the ground up and leave your mark on the next generation of Amazon robotics, this is the team to join.

- Bachelor's degree in Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field
- 7+ years of experience in technical lab, robotics, electro-mechanical, or automation environments, including operating, testing, and maintaining equipment
- 3+ years of experience leading or managing technical teams or lab/test operations
- Experience planning and executing hardware or physical system test or experimentation campaigns in partnership with cross-functional engineering teams
- Experience managing lab resources, equipment, supplies, and operational processes across one or more lab environments
- Experience troubleshooting, diagnosing, and maintaining electro-mechanical systems, control systems (e.g., PLC, I/O), or lab equipment
- Experience interpreting engineering documentation, including CAD, drawings, schematics, equipment specifications, test procedures, and/or Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)
- Experience with project management of technical projects, including scheduling, tracking, and documentation
Preferred qualifications: - Knowledge of Python and/or C++ programming
- Master's degree in Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Computer Science, or a related field
- Experience managing robotics, mechatronics, or system-level test labs across multiple physical locations
- Experience designing and implementing test request intake, prioritization, and scheduling systems or workflows
- Experience standing up new lab or test spaces, including equipment sourcing, installation, and calibration
- Experience operating, maintaining, and troubleshooting optical motion capture systems (e.g., OptiTrack, Vicon, or similar platforms)

- Experience developing teams and growing technical staff, including mentorship and shift/on-call coverage planning
- Experience communicating with users, technical teams, and management to collect requirements, evaluate alternatives, and develop supporting processes and tools

title: WW Tech Leader, Games TFC, AWS for Games
description:
Are you passionate about the games industry and ready to shape how game studios and publishers build on the cloud? AWS is looking for a Worldwide Technical Leader to own the global technical direction for the Games sub-industry within the Media, Entertainment, Games, and Sports (MEGS) organization. In this role, you will operate as the industry domain technical strategist, coordinating with business leadership to translate strategy into community action across a global Technical Field Community (TFC).
This is a dedicated individual contributor leadership role with no direct reports. You will lead through influence, earning the trust of community members across organizations and mobilizing them toward shared priorities. Your work will include prioritizing the use cases that matter most to games customers, organizing builders to create reusable solutions, resolving industry-specific technical requests at scale, incubating technical content, representing AWS at major games industry events, and growing the next generation of games specialists across the field. Success in this role means games customers get the right solutions faster, account teams are equipped to win, and AWS strengthens its position as the platform of choice for the games industry.
Key job responsibilities
- Own the global technical direction for the Games community, partnering with business leadership to align field insights to strategy, prioritizing use cases and customer needs that guide the technical field community outputs.
- Serve as the technical voice of the games market to AWS service teams, product managers, and go-to-market leaders, gathering customer pain points, emerging trends, and competitive intelligence from field engagements and translating them into structured product and roadmap input.
- Drive the creation and scaling of reusable technical artifacts — solutions, workshops, reference architectures, and guidance packages — aligned to prioritized games use cases, and set the quality bar for all games-related technical content published by the community.
- Lead AWS technical presence at major games industry events such as GDC, Gamescom, and re:Invent, owning session strategy, delivering keynotes, and engaging executive-level stakeholders at strategic games customers and partners.
- Grow and scale games industry expertise across the field by packaging successful customer engagements into repeatable solution architectures, sponsoring onboarding pathways, and mentoring generalist solutions architects into credible games practitioners.
A day in the life
You might start your morning reviewing account plans with a regional lead to identify where games customers need deeper technical engagement, then join a sync with service leadership to share field feedback on a product roadmap. After lunch, you could be reviewing a reference architecture that a community member built for a game backend use case, providing guidance before it gets published. Later, you are preparing keynote content for an upcoming industry conference and connecting with an account team to help shape a technical win strategy for a strategic customer evaluation.
About the team
The MEGS team operates four industry-aligned Technical Field Communities (Media & Entertainment, Games, Advertising & Marketing Technology, and Betting & Gaming). These communities are the connective tissue between deep domain expertise and field execution at scale. Leadership for the Games Technical Field Community sits within MEGS and brings together the builders from cross cutting technical organizations across AWS who share a passion for the games industry and converge around shared industry challenges to solve customer challenges with field scalable solutions. Our closest partners include the Games sub-industry business leader, AWS service teams, product marketing, go-to-market and account teams worldwide. If you want to combine deep games industry knowledge with the reach and resources of AWS to help customers build what is next, we would love to hear from you.

- Experience communicating across technical and non-technical audiences and at C-level, including training, workshops, publications
- Experience with Unity, Unreal, CryEngine, Lumberyard or proprietary 3D game engine, or industry-equivalent technology (3D animation, simulation, etc), or experience in Games Industry (supporting title Development, Release, or Live Ops)
- Experience in Games Industry (supporting title Development, Release, or Live Ops), or experience designing or architecting (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems

description:
Data Analysis Manager - Analytics & Transformation
At Capital One, data is at the center of everything we do. When we launched as a startup we disrupted the credit card industry by individually personalizing every credit card offer using statistical modeling and the relational database, cutting edge technology in 1988! Fast-forward a few years, and this little innovation and our passion for data has skyrocketed us to a Fortune 200 company and a leader in the world of data-driven decision-making.
The Enterprise Data team is focused on maximizing the value of our data ecosystem and enabling real-time, intelligent experiences built on a scalable, future ready foundation. We are a highly collaborative, cross-functional team working across Product, Technology, Design, Risk, and other partners to build a modern enterprise data ecosystem.
We are looking for an exceptional and innovative Data Analysis Manager to solve complex business and product challenges across our Enterprise Data Product teams. You will lead Product Analytics to measure and improve the performance and health of our Products and Platforms, transforming complex data into actionable, AI-enabled insights that shape product strategy and drive better decisions. If you are a strategic thinker who thrives on solving complex problems and using Data and AI to influence product development, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact.

Drive current and future strategy by leveraging your analytical skills
Assist with building and using models to test and validate data
Work with vast amounts of data in new and evolving environments
Be a part of growing and developing our brand in new and emerging markets
Leverage analytics to create a customer experience above our peers
Lead a team of talented junior analysts on an exciting professional journey while mentoring them and elevating their careers

Collaborate across business units
Work with top talent in a fast paced, entrepreneurial environment where analytics and good data are a top priority

Mining data to arrive at specific and crucial information for the organization
Identifying and implementing process, data, and reporting improvements for the organization
Working with large and complex databases containing millions to billions of records
Improving operational efficiencies and effectiveness
Conducting analysis to evaluate processes and tests
Extracting and analyzing data to gauge product offerings
Consulting on the design and implementation of new production and data storage systems
Developing and implementing strategic tests of products, initiatives and marketing materials
An ideal candidate will be on the leading edge of Analytical technology with a passion for the newest and most innovative tools. Possessing strong problem solving and conceptual thinking abilities in addition to communication, interpersonal and leadership skills are also important. title: Data Engineer 5
description:
Data Engineer 5
Do you love building and pioneering in the technology space? Do you enjoy solving complex business problems in a fast-paced, collaborative, inclusive and iterative delivery environment? At Capital One, you'll be part of a big group of makers, breakers, doers and disruptors who solve real problems and meet real customer needs. We are seeking Data Engineers who are passionate about marrying data with emerging technologies. In this role, you’ll be at the forefront of driving a major transformation across Capital One.
What You’ll Do:
Collaborate with and across Agile teams to design, develop, test, implement, and support technical solutions in full-stack development tools and technologies
Influence a team of developers, data analysts and data scientists with deep experience in machine learning, distributed microservices, lakehouse architecture, and full-stack systems
Utilize programming languages such as Python and Spark, along with open-source relational and NoSQL databases, and cloud-based data warehousing platforms including Databricks and Snowflake
Share your passion for staying on top of trends in data, experimenting with and learning new technologies, participating in internal and external technology communities, and mentoring other members of the data community
Collaborate with product managers and software engineers to deliver robust cloud-first data solutions that drive powerful experiences to help millions of Americans achieve financial empowerment
Independently design, build and deliver world-class cloud data solutions and applications with little or no support from supervisors or managers
Architect and enforce common data engineering design patterns to ensure code quality, maintainability, and reusability across data platforms and pipelines
Serve as an ambassador for the data engineering team, communicating technical concepts and data outcomes clearly to both internal and external stakeholders to drive alignment and shared understanding
Design and build data pipelines and platforms with a focus on scalability, resilience, and operational efficiency, ensuring robust performance under increasing data volume and business demands
Serve as a force-multiplier for the team, balancing deep, hands-on technical contribution and innovation with mentoring and elevating the skills of peers and junior engineers
Lead and execute large-scale, transformative data initiatives from end to end, independently driving critical architectural decisions and evaluating platform choices, such as Snowflake versus Databricks, based on technical and business requirements
Basic Qualifications:
Bachelor's Degree or higher in Computer Science or a related quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Engineering)
At least 6 years of experience in application development (Internship experience does not apply)
At least 4 years of experience in distributed data
At least 4 years of experience with SQL
At least 4 years of experience programming with at least one of the following languages: Python, Java, or Scala
At least 4 years of experience designing and developing data pipelines
At least 2 years of experience in data modeling and designing end-to-end data solutions using both relational and non-relational database systems
Preferred Qualifications:
Master’s Degree in Computer Science or a related field
8+ years of experience in data engineering
4+ years of data modeling experience
9+ years of experience in application development with demonstrated proficiency in Python, SQL, Scala, or Java
5+ years of hands-on experience designing, deploying and operating data workloads in at least one public cloud environment (AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud)
5+ years of experience building or supporting distributed data or compute workloads using tools such as EMR, Spark, Glue, or Databricks
5+ years of experience designing, implementing, and operating real-time or streaming data pipelines
3+ years of experience working on data observability (e.g., Monte Carlo, Splunk) or data orchestration tools (e.g., Airflow, Dagster)
5+ years of experience working with unstructured or semistructured data using NoSQL databases (e.g., MongoDB, Cassandra, DynamoDB)
5+ years of experience designing and supporting data warehousing solutions (e.g., Snowflake, Redshift)
3+ years of experience working in an Agile development environment
3+ years of experience developing user-centric reusable data products

description:
Director - Ecosystem Risk & Integrity - High Brand Risk & Prohibited Investigations
As a Director in Capital One’s Ecosystem Risk & Integrity organization, you will apply your visionary leadership and analytical prowess to safeguard our Global Payments Ecosystem. Leading our High Brand Risk (HBR) and Prohibited Activity Monitoring programs, you will act as a critical first line of defense, working across the enterprise to develop and implement cutting-edge transaction monitoring solutions. In this high-profile role, you will lead a dynamic team of Risk Specialists to ensure participants uphold our network standards and comply with evolving domestic and international regulatory requirements.
Directors in Capital One’s Risk Management organization partner with Executives, network partners, and cross-functional teams to drive organizational change. You will spearhead the modernization of our capabilities to better manage the Company’s risk in an open, collaborative environment where innovative ideas and robust solutions are both welcomed and rewarded.
You are a highly motivated Risk Management professional with a passion for payments integrity, excellent organizational leadership, and strong communication skills. You will have a high level of exposure across lines of business and the opportunity to work directly with Executives to create resilient, forward-thinking strategies. By evaluating "gray area" activities, detecting transaction laundering, and enforcing noncompliance controls, you will identify and mitigate potential reputational, legal, and regulatory risks to the Company while empowering smart, sustainable business growth.
Core Responsibilities
Integrate Intelligence to Critical Risk Processes: Work with business partners, acquiring participants, and external vendor partnerships (e.g., G2, LegitScript) to validate and execute transaction monitoring processes that protect network integrity and the company's bottom line.  Widen our intelligence aperture to bring in new signals from new providers and implement a clear A/B testing protocol for 3rd party partnerships.
Consult & Collaborate: Consult with Executives to determine the optimal interaction model with Payment Schemes and external participants, fostering positive relationships, proactive registration outreach, and transparent compliance standards.
Programmatic Uplift and Framework Development: Drive the strategic finalization of the High Brand Risk (HBR) category and sub-category framework. You will establish risk tolerance guardrails for complex merchant activities (e.g., skill-based gaming, online gambling, adult content, regulated products, digital currency).  Contour and implement enforcement protocol and compliance standards across our
Anomaly Detection and Investigation: Perform critical assessments on network anomalies, deceptive practices, and transaction laundering to mitigate regulatory and reputational risk, ensuring strict adherence to Operating Regulations and mandates (e.g., UIGEA / Reg GG), as well as elevated laws and regulations in areas which pose increased risk.
Extensive Gap Assessments: Perform extensive gap assessments on legacy transaction monitoring tools and investigation workflows. Create technology integration requirements to ensure scalable, data-driven business decisions across HBR and Prohibited Investigations processes, tools, and platforms.
Drive Process Excellence: Use advanced analytical skills to assess and improve processes and operations.  Focus on automating logic-based rules, refining referral sources, and standardizing noncompliance fee assessment decision trees.
Scale Governance & Oversight: Drive large-scale Process Management and Governance, overseeing Quality Assurance frameworks, acquirer monitoring programs, compliance attestations, and executive reporting.
Empower Dynamic Teams: Lead and develop multifaceted teams segmented across Strategy, Program Administration, Investigations, and Operations. Foster a culture of professional growth, ownership, and cross-functional resilience.

Bachelor's degree or military experience
At least 5 years of experience in Project Management or Process Management

Master's degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Economics, Mathematics, or Project Management
At least 6 years of experience as a project manager or process manager within financial services or global payments, specifically in anti-money laundering, fraud, or transaction monitoring
At least 10 years of overall experience as a project manager or process manager
Experience managing international payments or fintech operations across multiple regions
Business Process Management certification, Lean Six Sigma Green Belt certification, Lean Six Sigma Black Belt certification, Agile Coach certification, or Certified Regulatory Compliance Manager certification

Director of Hospitality, Retail Experiences
Capital One, a Fortune 500 company and one of the nation’s top 10 banks, offers a broad spectrum of financial products and services to consumers, small businesses and commercial clients. Our mission is to create one of the nation’s great banks, and we have the necessary ingredients: a strong balance sheet, resilient businesses, a massive customer franchise, strong analytical capabilities, and great people. We nurture a work environment where people with a variety of thoughts, ideas and backgrounds, guided by our shared Values, come together to make Capital One a great company – and a great place to work.
The Role:
We are looking for a Director of Hospitality to lead the customer-facing, multi-unit food and beverage program in our nationwide Capital One Café network.  In this high impact role, you’ll set the vision and strategy around food and beverage offerings, promotional/marketing plans, and frontline readiness, partnering closely with Visual Merchandising, Marketing, Programming and others to bring this vision to life. Additionally, you will manage the performance of our third-party operator and coffee partner, and lead an internal team of ~5-7 associates. You will be responsible for turning the CX strategy into reality and building a scalable program to support our growing network.  You’ll operate in a collaborative environment that values your insight, encourages continuous learning, and rewards innovation.
Key Responsibilities:
Food & Beverage (F&B) Program Strategy & Operations
Program Vision: Lead the vision for the Capital One Café F&B program, ensuring alignment with our broader Retail Experience strategy.
Menu & Offering Innovation: Develop and evolve F&B menu offerings to meet evolving customer needs.
Operational Excellence: Set and maintain rigorous operating standards and standard operating procedures (SOPs) to ensure consistent, premium guest experiences across the nationwide network.
Strategy Execution: Drive work around frontline readiness, promotional and marketing plans, and operational adjustments to maximize efficiency and customer satisfaction.
Partner & Vendor Management
Vendor Performance: Own the end-to-end relationship and performance metrics for our third-party food and beverage operator; define and enforce partner financial reporting standards and staffing guidelines.
Quality Assurance: Oversee network performance through regular analysis of customer feedback, mystery shopping, and operational audits to ensure excellence in delivery.
Contract Governance: Manage operational accountability and service-level agreements (SLAs) with external partners.
Cross-Functional Leadership
Strategic Collaboration: Provide tactical and strategic thought partnership to leaders across Retail Design, Marketing, Strategy, Product, and the Frontline to ensure the hospitality experience is seamlessly integrated into the overall Capital One Café customer experience.
Marketing Integration: Work closely with internal marketing and PR teams to craft and amplify the guest experience story and Café promotional programming.
Events and Programming Integration: Provide strategic alignment and F&B integration into seasonal campaigns, in-cafe events, promotions, and programming on an ongoing basis.
Team Business Operations
People Leadership: Lead, develop, and coach a high-performing internal team, fostering a culture of continuous learning, collaboration, and innovation.
Financial & Resource Management: Manage the F&B program budget, balancing the need to elevate the guest experience while finding cost efficiencies and driving overall profitability.
Performance Tracking: Own the alignment, tracking, and management of team KPIs and OKRs, driving regular business reviews with senior leadership
Basic Qualifications:
Bachelor’s Degree or Military experience
At least 5 Years of experience leading projects in a corporate or hospitality environment
At least 5 Years of people leadership experience
Preferred Qualifications:
7+ years of experience in strategic scaling of retail or hospitality operations in a multi-unit setting
Hospitality consulting experience in a high quality fast-casual environment
Proven experience in storytelling, deck building, and presenting in a leadership setting
Excellent problem solving and influencing skills

title: Full Time Branch Ambassador - MacArthur
description:
Full Time Branch Ambassador - MacArthur
Welcome to the future of banking. At Capital One, we believe your bank should be as mobile, intuitive, and human as the rest of your life. We are reimagining the way people interact with their money by creating community hubs where technology meets human empathy.
As a Branch Ambassador , you are the heartbeat of our space. You don't just "process transactions"—you embody our culture of outstanding hospitality. You are a relationship-builder who blends friendly, attentive service with cutting-edge digital innovation. Whether you’re helping a client navigate our latest tools or empowering them to reach their financial goals, you are the face of an exceptional, human-centric experience.
We are looking for curious, empathetic, and tech-savvy individuals who thrive in a fast-moving environment. You are someone who doesn't wait to be asked; you anticipate needs, solve problems before they arise, and have a genuine passion for helping people thrive in an evolving digital world.
What You’ll Actually Do
The Guardian of Trust & Accuracy You are the bedrock of our environment’s safety and integrity. You’ll execute high-volume cash transactions—including deposits, withdrawals, and complex negotiable instrument processing—with 100% accuracy. You maintain a "compliance-first" mindset, ensuring all security, audit, BSA/AML, and federal regulatory standards are met with precision to keep our customers' assets safe.
The Digital Concierge You are a mentor in a digital world. You’ll educate clients on how to leverage mobile banking, remote deposit capture, and contactless payments, helping them gain convenience and security in their daily financial lives.
The First-Line Consultant You aren’t just answering questions; you’re identifying needs. By actively listening, you’ll uncover personal or business goals and pair them with the right digital tools or banking solutions to help them succeed.
The Hospitality Lead You move fluidly throughout the space, greeting customers and ensuring no one ever feels like just a "number." You balance the efficiency of a high-volume operation with the warmth of a community-focused partner.
What You Bring
A Hospitality Heart: You have a natural gift for making people feel welcome and heard.
Tech Fluency: You are an early adopter of apps and digital tools and love teaching others how to use them.
Precision and Detail: You find satisfaction in getting the numbers right every single time and following clear procedures.
Adaptability: You enjoy a "fluid" workspace where you might move from a cash drawer to a digital demo in minutes.
Curiosity: You want to know the "why" behind the "how" and are always looking for ways to improve the customer journey.
Why Join Us?
This isn't just a job—it’s work with a mission. Because we’ve removed the pressure of traditional sales quotas, you are free to focus on the depth of your impact on customers, teammates, and the community. We provide an inclusive environment where we invest in your confidence, service mindset, and professional growth. We ensure you have the tools to be stronger in your role and more effective in how you show up every day.
The Perks
We provide a comprehensive benefits package designed to fuel your journey. Whether you’re using our education assistance to prepare for your next career move, or taking advantage of our mental and physical health resources to stay at your best, we invest in you as a whole person. Our goal is to ensure that wherever your career takes you—within Capital One or into the wider world—you leave the Branch stronger than when you started.
Day 1 coverage for Medical, Dental, Vision and Prescriptions, plus Flexible Spending Accounts, Life and Disability Insurance
Paid Time Off
Education Assistance
Matching 401(k) contribution up to 7.5%
Paid Parental Leave
Mental Health support
Back-up Child or Elder Care
And much more!
Essential Functions (Included, but not limited to)
Support surrounding Branches as needed within a 50 mile radius, with occasional opportunities to assist other locations in the broader Region.
Available to work a flexible schedule, including nights, weekends, with hours and days subject to change.
While the company provides reasonable notice for permanent schedule changes in accordance with state and local laws, the ability to adapt to business-driven schedule adjustments is required.
Applicants must be able to attend all required training sessions, which may occur on a schedule differing from the primary shift.
Lifting up to 25 pounds and moving/standing for extended periods of time
Regular and consistent attendance
Basic Qualifications
High School Diploma, GED, or Equivalent Certification
At least 1 year of Retail, Sales, or Customer Service experience
At least 6 months of cash handling experience
Preferred Qualifications
Associate’s degree
2+ years of Retail or Customer-facing experience
Proficient in G-Suite
Strong written and oral communication skills
After you apply
You may be required to take an assessment. It takes about 35 minutes to complete. If you’re selected to move forward, one of our recruiters will reach out to tell you more about the role and answer your questions.
Does this sound like the career move you’ve been looking for? Let’s build the future of banking together!

At Capital One, data is at the center of everything we do. As part of our newly formed Centralized Card Data Team , we sit at the top of the Card Product Controllers (CPC) organization and act as the definitive voice for all Card Accounting data needs. We are bridging the gap between raw data infrastructure and downstream financial reporting, turning data management from a back-office task into a core strategic advantage.
As a Principal Associate on the Card Data Team, you will leverage your data governance and strategic skills to provide early leadership on fast-moving data projects and provide leadership. You will act as an embedded Business Steward, balancing the need to accelerate our digital transformation with the need to follow strict regulatory frameworks.
On any given day you will be challenged by three types of work – Data Stewardship, Data Governance, and Operations:
Data Stewardship & Consultation
Partner Across Teams: Serve as the primary liaison and data contact for the Card Product Controllers team, working closely with technical and business teams.
Strategic Guidance: Provide early consultation on major enterprise initiatives to guarantee Card-specific accounting requirements are addressed.
Business Stewardship: Focus on "Trust" and "Compliance" by defining data meaning and usage, while partnering closely with Technical Data Stewards who handle storage and movement.
​
Data Governance & Management
Quality Processes: Establish and run standardized processes for data quality protocols, profiling, and defining Critical Data Elements and usage.
Data Delivery Agreements: Help define operational contracts, Data Provisioning Agreements (DPAs), and SLAs (covering delivery times, cadence, and source system cut-offs) to streamline downstream consumption.
​
Operations & Knowledge Management
Risk Reduction: Promote a controlled change management environment to reduce data risk and eliminate the manual overhead spent investigating "out-of-balance" exceptions. Performing outage audits/retros to identify data improvement opportunities that can limit our speed to market strategy.
Team Advocacy: Serve as the definitive voice for the team, educating consumers on new data standards, supporting operational integration with the Speed to Market team, and preparing executive updates.
​
Our ideal candidate will have:
A high level of comfort operating independently in an ambiguous, "startup-like" environment within a newly formed team.
The ability to tackle big foundational tasks from scratch, such as establishing dataset inventories and data quality rules.
Strong communication skills to translate complex technical constraints into clear business impacts, and vice versa.
The ability to build trust and influence cross-functional partners, including Product Owners, Tech, and Financial Data Management.
Basic Qualifications:
Bachelor's Degree or military experience
At least 3 years of experience in accounting, external financial reporting, audit, finance, or a combination

Master’s Degree in Finance, Analytics, or a related quantitative field
Certified Public Accountant (CPA) license or Project Management Professional (PMP) designation
5+ years of progressive experience working in data analytics, data governance, business intelligence, or financial data systems
4+ years of experience working directly within a financial institution, supporting Product Controllers, Finance or general ledger data infrastructure

Familiarity with Agile operating models, writing logical rules and requirements, and integrating data controls directly into a delivery pipeline

description:
Principal Associate, Data Scientist - People Strategy & Analytics
Data is at the center of everything we do. As a startup, we disrupted the credit card industry by individually personalizing every credit card offer using statistical modeling and the relational database, cutting edge technology in 1988! Fast-forward a few years, and this little innovation and our passion for data has skyrocketed us to a Fortune 200 company and a leader in the world of data-driven decision-making.
As a Data Scientist at Capital One, you’ll be part of a team that’s leading the next wave of disruption at a whole new scale, using the latest in computing and machine learning technologies and operating across billions of customer records to unlock the big opportunities that help everyday people save money, time and agony in their financial lives.
Team Description
People Strategy & Analytics brings data, analytics, and insights to shape critical talent decisions and strategy at Capital One. We work closely with HR partners and senior executives in shaping talent policy, automating real-time data, and improving talent decision-making. The team is comprised of people with diverse skills and backgrounds including: data analysts, data scientists, business analysts, HR specialists, project managers, and industrial/organizational psychologists.
As a Data Scientist on Capital One’s People Strategy & Analytics team, you’ll be on the leading edge of applying analytics to talent, combining artificial intelligence, machine learning, and social science to build models that seek to understand associate behavior, improve HR efficiency and tools, and inform strategies aimed at expanding Capital One’s talent advantage.
Role Description
In this role, you will:
Build natural language processing and machine learning models through all phases of development, from design through training, evaluation, validation, and implementation
Apply expertise in using open source large language models (LLMs) through prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and evaluation metric frameworks for business specific applications
Partner with a cross-functional team of data scientists, software engineers, business analysts, and product managers to deliver industry leading HR tools and AI-powered products
Leverage a broad stack of technologies — Python, SQL, AWS, LangChain, Hugging Face Transformers, VectorDBs, Pytorch/TensorFlow, and more — to reveal the insights hidden within large volumes of numeric and textual data
Flex your interpersonal skills to collaborate with internal stakeholders, translating complex data science work into tangible, aligned business outcomes.
The Ideal Candidate is:
Passionate about human capital: You are excited by the value we can add to our company and our associates, and are inspired to help make a large positive impact.
Innovative. You continually research and evaluate emerging technologies. You stay current on published state-of-the-art methods, technologies, and applications and seek out opportunities to apply them.
Creative. You thrive on bringing definition to big, undefined problems. You love asking questions and pushing hard to find answers. You’re not afraid to share a new idea.
Technical. You’re comfortable with open-source languages and are passionate about developing further. You have hands-on experience developing data science solutions using open-source tools and cloud computing platforms.
Statistically-minded. You’ve built models, validated them, and backtested them. You know how to interpret a confusion matrix or a ROC curve. You have experience with clustering, classification, sentiment analysis, time series, and deep learning.

A Bachelor's Degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field) plus 5 years of experience performing data analytics
A Master's Degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field) plus 3 years of experience performing data analytics
A PhD in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field)

Master’s Degree in “STEM” field (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics) plus 3 years of experience in data analytics, or PhD in “STEM” field (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics)
At least 1 year of experience working with AWS
At least 3 years’ experience in Python
At least 3 years’ experience with machine learning
At least 3 years’ experience with SQL
