title: Store Manager - Bench
description:
What You Will Do
All Lowe’s associates deliver quality customer service while maintaining a store that is clean, safe, and stocked with the products our customers need. As a Store Manager, this means:
• Ensuring associates are delivering friendly, professional and timely service to all customers who shop the store.
• Monitoring the performance, profitability, and flow-through of store plans and programs.
• Championing and implementing strategic asset protection plans that improve safety and security outcomes.
The Store Manager manages the overall store operations (i.e., expenses, merchandising standards, compliance, safety, security, and workforce) and those directly helping customers to drive positive customer experiences, sales, and margin performance. The Store Manager works closely with cross-functional partners in HR, Asset Protection, and Operations at the District, Region, and Corporate levels to execute the Lowe’s business strategy within his/her store.
To be successful, the Store Manager must build and support a store culture, in partnership with key stakeholders, that is aligned to the Lowe’s mission and behaviors where employees are engaged and inspired. This leader is also responsible for maintaining a strategic view of store talent needs, recruiting and developing talent, driving execution of sales and service strategies, analyzing relevant data to inform store-specific strategies, championing customer service, proactively addressing store needs, and acting as the Lowe’s brand ambassador for the community.
Travel Requirements: This role does not require regular travel; however, this role may need to travel on occasion to meetings, trainings, or to support neighboring stores.
What We're Looking For
• Salaried: Generally scheduled for 48 hours; more hours may be required based on the needs of the business.
• Requires morning, afternoon and evening availability any day of the week.
• Physical ability to perform tasks that may require prolonged standing, sitting, and other activities necessary to perform job duties.
• Minimally must be able to lift 25 pounds without assistance; may lift over 25 pounds with or without assistance.
What You Need To Succeed
Minimum Qualifications
• Bachelor’s degree and 3 years of experience leading associates in a large retail environment, with Sales Volume exceeding 20M annually OR 5 years of experience leading associates in a large retail environment, with Sales Volume exceeding 20M annually.
• 5 years of experience working in a fast-paced, cross-functional work environment.
• Experience building and maintaining cross-functional relationships in a matrixed environment.
• Experience building partnerships within the community.
• Experience analyzing and using customer, market, and competitor data to inform decisions and business planning.
• Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite.

• Bachelor’s Degree in business administration, marketing, or related field.
• Experience managing in big‐box Home Improvement retail industry.

title: Supply Chain, Lead Analyst
description:
Do your Best Work in Mooresville
This position is based at our headquarters in Mooresville, North Carolina. Our corporate office is a space where you can collaborate and do your best work. Take a walk, grab a bite (or a cup of coffee), work out or get a check-up – we invest in you so you can find your inspiration.
Your Impact
The Supply Chain, Lead Analyst supports the delivery of the objectives of Supply Chain in providing operational consistency and initiative success to the overall Supply Chain organization. This role provides analytical support to initiative and operational leadership within the Supply Chain team while also assuming responsibility for the delivery of tactical initiatives. This role operates with a high level of cross-functional collaboration across Supply Chain as well as with other enterprise functions (Store Operations, Merchandising, Tech, Finance, and others) and external partners.
What You Will Do Performs detailed analysis (quantitative and qualitative) to support the development of Supply Chain capabilities.
Analyzes Supply Chain data and provides actionable performance recommendations to leadership.
Facilitates identification of operational issues to analyze and reveal trends; supports timely resolution of issues impacting operational execution.
Develops reporting and tracking mechanisms/tools to track performance of Supply Chain initiatives against Objectives and Key Results (OKRs), including summarized performance views as needed.
Supports development and tracking of project plans to ensure timely delivery of desired outputs.
Identifies risks to strategic Supply Chain initiatives and supports the development of risk mitigation plans.
Manages cross-functional relationships enabling successful implementation of Supply Chain initiatives.
Develops and/or oversees execution of change management plans to drive initiative adoption, including facilitating onsite or virtual training sessions when needed.
Collects post-project or post-event feedback to support continuous improvement solutions.
Performs ad hoc competitive and market analysis.
Serves as project manager when needed; communicates frequently to Project Sponsors/Business leads and stakeholders on status, issues, risks, lessons learned, and accomplishments.
Supports the Supply Chain portfolio intake process as needed.
Analyzes operational problems and implements analytics solutions enabling business improvements through modeling, analytical reviews, data mining, and other analytical methods.
Acts as a subject matter expert and liaison for cross-functional efforts; assists with design and development of value-added operational reporting and analysis across Supply Chain.
Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, or related field or equivalent years of experience in lieu of education requirement, if applicable
7+ years of overall experience in supply chain, logistics, operations, analytics, or project coordination roles, preferably in a retail, e-commerce, or distribution setting.
7+ years strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to translate data into business insights.
7+ years ability to manage work across multiple projects and teams in a fast-paced environment.
3-5 years proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint; experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau).
3-5 years strong problem-solving and critical-thinking skills.
3-5 years strong interpersonal and written/verbal communication skills.
3-5 years high level of initiative and ability to work independently and collaboratively.
Preferred Skills/Education Familiarity with retail or e-commerce supply chain environments.
Lean Six Sigma Certification-IASSC

Within our warehouse team, you play a key role in making sure our products are accurately received, organized, and shipped. As part of a team dedicated to delivering excellence in supply chain operations, your work directly affects our success in achieving our mission.

Your Day at Lowe's
As a warehouse Team Member, you'll build a range of skills and play a crucial role in ensuring that our stores, customers, and communities receive the products they need. You will be expected to consistently perform your tasks efficiently and work with others as part of a team. In addition, all team members are expected to follow safety regulations and procedures.
Team Members work in diverse departments, each contributing to our supply chain operations. These departments include Building, Shipping, and Receiving.
Key Responsibilities
Receive, organize, and ship products accurately and efficiently.
Prioritize safety by adhering to proper procedures and conventions.
Perform tasks in various departments as assigned by the Operations Supervisor.
Conduct safety inspections of equipment and adhere to safety regulations.
Minimum Qualifications
Team members may work evening, overnight, and weekend shifts, with voluntary and scheduled overtime as needed (additional pay for overtime).
Physical fitness to move continuously throughout the facility, lift up to 70 pounds, and operate power equipment.
Adherence to safety protocols, wearing necessary personal protective equipment.
Ability to work in varying conditions, from extreme temperatures to noisy environments.
Strong safety orientation and ability to work independently or within a team.
Preferred Qualifications
High school diploma or GED equivalent.
Previous experience in distribution center operations or warehouse settings.
Proficiency in operating power equipment (e.g., forklift, reach truck).
Detail-oriented with experience in a fast-paced environment.
Basic math, reading comprehension, and computer skills.
Spatial reasoning for effective product positioning.
Shift Schedule
This location has the greatest need for the below shifts:
Night Shift: Monday-Thursday 6pm-4:30am
Weekends: Friday-Sunday 6am-6:30pm
Working Conditions
Environmental factors vary by location. You may be working in both inside and outside weather conditions. Exposure to varying climates, including extreme heat or cold, wet, damp, humid, windy, or drafty conditions, is possible. You may be exposed to constant or intermittent noises in addition to moving or shaking objects and equipment.
Lifting methods vary based on role, weight, and volume. Associates must follow guidelines, limiting single lifts to 70 pounds. Team lifts are used minimally starting at 70 pounds or when needed. Powered equipment should be used as required, with proper training or assistance from a trained coworker.

title: Transportation Clerk - Team Member
description:
What You Will Do
The IDC Transportation Clerk is primarily responsible administrative work and direct support for handling inbound and outbound drivers at the Distribution Center’s Transportation Center. This role is responsible for administrative tasks related to dedicated carriers, inbound and outbound loads, and a variety of activities supporting transportation. These activities include maintaining physical documents, scheduling inbound live appointments, and corresponding with carriers to keep daily backhaul information up to date. This role processes the paperwork for drivers, receives product in the Data Management System (DMS) and prepares shipping documents for outbound trucks. The individual in this role is expected to provide exemplary customer service and serves as “the face of Lowe’s” to drivers who enter the facility grounds. In addition, this role is responsible for coordinating traffic on the facility yard and monitoring movements of trailers from and to the docks.

• Demonstrated track record of good attendance

• Basic computer skills including a working knowledge of Microsoft Office

• Demonstrated track record of consistent and reliable on-the-job contribution

• Experience operating power equipment (e.g., forklift, reach truck, yard truck)

description:
Your Impact
The Warehouse Associate II is primarily responsible for working in our Receiving department, picking, pulling, receiving, labeling, and stocking purchase orders within the specified amount of time. The Warehouse Associate II is responsible for handling product safely and in accordance with best methods to maintain product quality.
What You Will Do
Uses power equipment (e.g., forklift) to unload deliveries for trucks, organizing and storing received items in appropriate areas
Efficiently and accurately receive purchase orders, checking for damaging and comparing purchase orders with invoices and/or packaging lists
Accurately pulls products from warehouse shelves based on item number, size, color, and quantity requirements
Packs and stages completed purchase orders for delivery
Verifies accuracy of items picked from warehouse shelves and staged for delivery by other warehouse associates
Achieves or exceeds performance expectations by completing all receiving tasks efficiently and effectively
Trained and performs tasks in cross-functional areas, such as picking, pulling, labeling, shipping, and/or helping with deliveries, as assigned by management

The Sr Manager, Growth AI Transformation will work directly with the Global Head AI Transformation to identify, develop, and scale AI-powered initiatives across the Global Growth function and across regional and local markets worldwide.

This isn't a factory-floor quality role; this is a strategic, division-level opportunity to be the central nervous system for food safety. As our Sr. Specialist, you are the designated Subject Matter Expert for the most critical risks to our products and consumers:   allergens, chemical hazards, and foreign materials.   You won't be responsible for a single lab or plant; instead, you'll be the expert who provides the guidance, sets the standards, and builds the risk frameworks that our internal and external manufacturing partners across the entire Accelerator portfolio execute against. You are the technical authority who ensures our sites are compliant, our testing is robust, and our products are safe, no matter where they're made.
What You’ll Do (Key Responsibilities)
Govern Food Safety Standards:   Own the Accelerator Allergen Substantiation procedure, govern division-level chemical and mycotoxin hazard controls, and support compliance with the Mars Foreign Material Management Standard (FMMS).
Act as the SME:   Provide expert technical guidance for site-level risk assessments, support sites in achieving compliance, and act as the division SME for any contamination incidents (PRIMPs), guiding investigations and CAPA development.
Drive Continuous Improvement:   Identify and lead initiatives within the allergen, chemical, and foreign material domains to drive risk reduction, improve testing efficiency, and optimize costs.
Manage Risk & Verification:   Lead and maintain Division Quality Risk Management activities within the Archer platform. Partner on lab test trending and study execution to refine verification requirements for finished products.
Deploy Technology & Training:   Lead the deployment and governance of the handheld XRF analyzer program across internal sites and develop specialized training programs to build expertise across the network.
Represent the Division:   Serve as the Accelerator representative in relevant Mars Global Communities of Practice, influencing global strategy to support our division's needs and future growth.
What We’re Looking For
A Deep Technical Expert:   Advanced, practical knowledge of food safety hazards, specifically allergens (risk assessments, testing, changeovers), chemical contaminants, and foreign material control (metal detection, X-ray).
A Strategic Standard-Setter:   Experience developing and implementing guidance, specifications, and risk frameworks for manufacturing sites to execute against, rather than just following established procedures.
An Influential Collaborator:   The ability to provide expert guidance and drive compliance across a network of internal sites and co-manufacturers without direct authority.
A Proven Problem-Solver:   Demonstrable experience in root-cause analysis, incident management (PRIMP), and developing corrective/preventive action plans (CAPA).
Qualifications
Education:   Bachelor’s degree in Food Science, Chemistry, Biology, or a closely related field.
Experience:   7+ years of experience in a food manufacturing environment with a focus on quality and food safety.
Certifications:   HACCP, FSSC 22000 (or similar GFSI scheme) certification required. Certified auditor experience is also required.
Location:   Must be based in the Chicago, IL area.
Travel:   Ability to travel up to 30% to manufacturing sites.

AI Cloud Data Storage
NVIDIA DGXC Storage org handles some of the fastest training and inference tasks. Every GPU cycle depends on a storage platform built to keep tens of thousands of accelerators continuously busy. It maintains exabytes of data securely and powers the largest AI workloads worldwide across cloud, neocloud, and on-prem setups. With the growth of accelerated computing, storage is essential. It can make the difference between effective GPU use and wasted potential and between launching a frontier model on time or missing the deadline by months. We seek a Distinguished Engineer to lead NVIDIA's storage strategy for AI Cloud across the Neocloud Provider (NCP) and Cloud Service Provider (CSP) ecosystem. You will direct the architecture of high-performance parallel file systems, object stores, and block storage at exabyte scale. You will stay hands-on, collaborating with engineers, SREs, partners, and storage vendors. You will apply NVIDIA's AI tools to increase your productivity and that of those you impact. This is a distinctive prospect to establish the storage framework of the AI era at the company that introduced accelerated computing.
What you'll be doing:
Lead the multi-year technical plan for AI Cloud Storage expansion across NCPs — determine the reference architecture, capabilities, performance and durability SLOs, qualification methodology, and roadmap for the high-performance file, object, and block storage that each NCP must offer to qualify for NVIDIA GPU allocation.
Serve as the chief storage architect with deep hands-on involvement. Lead key reviews of storage builds and investigate root causes of complex production problems. Develop prototype reference implementations to minimize risks in new initiatives. Make final technical decisions on NCP storage deliveries using measurable SLOs. Apply AI tools heavily to amplify your technical influence throughout the program.
Define the standard for "production-ready" in NCP storage, including durability and availability SLOs measured in 9s. Ensure sustained efficiency per TiB, observability, blast-radius containment, and reduced operational toil. Influence GPU delivery gating by requiring AI Cloud to accept GPU capacity only after verifying storage-focused ancillary services.
Develop and guide the architectural direction by working closely with collaborators in training, inference, and accelerated-computing product lines. Coordinate with site-reliability, operations, networking, and security colleagues. Work together with external cloud providers, neocloud operators, and storage vendors to align on a common architecture.
Develop the open-source path forward for AI storage. Establish and guide an open-source strategy that broadens the AI storage ecosystem. Advocate for a GitHub-first, security-first stance. Engage deeply with upstream open-source communities. Formalize the APIs, SDKs, and protocols allowing partners and the industry to build, integrate, and create with NVIDIA at the AI storage level.
Lead an engineering culture centered on AI tools. Regularly use modern AI coding and agentic tools in your daily tasks. Show what 10× engineering means at NVIDIA. Distribute patterns, prompts, and evaluation harnesses across the storage organization.
Partner with peer Distinguished and Principal storage architects across the organization to tackle the most difficult, long-term technical challenges. Make automation the only acceptable solution for infrastructure management tasks like live software upgrades, node and drive replacements, capacity rebalancing, cross-DC data movement, and dataset lifecycle. Establish root-cause analysis and corrective action rigor on every major incident. Design the storage layer for workloads spanning the next several GPU generations, including disaggregated inference with storage-backed KV caching, large-scale write-once-read-many inference patterns, exabyte regional object stores, and cross-DC dataset versioning and copy management.
Mentor and develop senior, principal, and distinguished engineers across the storage organization and nearby business units. Raise the technical bar broadly. Represent NVIDIA externally in standards bodies, open-source communities, customer briefings, and industry forums (FAST, SC, OCP, SNIA, Linux Storage Summit).
What we need to see:
BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field — or equivalent experience.
A minimum of 18+ years of practical engineering experience in storage technology is needed. This involves extensive involvement with a high-performance parallel file system like Lustre, GPFS / Spectrum Scale, WEKA, VAST, BeeGFS, DAOS, or its equivalent, handling data at multi-petabyte scale. Candidates must also have wide-ranging expertise in object storage (S3 / Swift-class) and block storage (NVMe-oF, NVMesh-class, iSCSI).
A track record of crafting and managing storage platforms at exabyte scale for performance-critical workloads — AI training, HPC, video, or hyperscale data lakes — including direct responsibility for durability, availability, and performance SLOs measured in 9s.
Demonstrated ability to set technical strategy across business units and partner organizations. You have driven multi-year storage architectures adopted by multiple teams, vendors, or customers. You can point to measurable outcomes such as GPU utility lift, $/PB reduction, incidents eliminated, and time-to-bring-up compressed.
You are 100% hands-on in engineering. You write and review production code yourself. When a bug requires it, you read Lustre, NFS, kernel, NVMe-oF, or SPDK source code. You also run scale tests or recovery drills personally instead of delegating.
Strong proficiency in at least one systems language (C, C++, Rust, or Go) and proficiency in Python; comfortable in the Linux kernel storage and networking stacks (block layer, RDMA / RoCE / InfiniBand, NVMe, page cache, VFS, multipath).
Frequent daily use of advanced AI coding and autonomous tools, including specific examples showing how you accelerated building, coding, debugging, validation, and operations. Also, share your perspective on future trends.
Excellent written and verbal communication. You can write a one-pager that aligns a VP. You can also write a six-pager that aligns an entire org. You can explain a deep technical trade-off to an SRE, a vendor CTO, and an internal customer in the same week.
Comfort operating in a 24/7 production environment where storage incidents directly impact GPU revenue, with a security-first approach baked into every build.
Ways to stand out from the crowd:
Proven background in designing or managing storage solutions for AI training or inference at 10k+ GPU scale, demonstrating clear improvements in GPU utilization or reducing I/O bottlenecks.
Open-source contributions or maintainership in Lustre, NFS, SPDK, NVMe / NVMe-oF, CSI, Ceph, MinIO, RocksDB, or related projects.
Built or led a disaggregated-inference or Inference-Time-Compute storage architecture — KV caching to fast in-cluster or GPU-adjacent storage, WORM at scale, storage-aware scheduling, or database-integrated inference.
Public technical contributions — patents, peer-reviewed papers (FAST, SOSP, NSDI, OSDI, ATC), keynote talks, or RFCs — that demonstrate expertise and leadership in storage for AI infrastructure.
NVIDIA led the way in accelerated computing. Today, our AI infrastructure drives global intelligence, changing industries worldwide. The AI Cloud Storage group forms the base that maintains the world's largest GPU fleet's productivity. title: Head of Infrastructure Security Engineering - EDA Clusters
location: US, CA, Remote; US, MA, Westford; US, TX, Austin; US, WA, Remote; US, NC, Durham
description:
Securing NVIDIA’s EDA clusters is not a matter of deploying the standard security stack. These workloads are too large, too long-running, and too performance-sensitive for the off-the-shelf playbook to simply apply. That constraint is the job. We’re hiring an engineering leader to build and run Infrastructure Security Engineering for EDA Clusters : the team responsible for implementing security controls across the compute, storage, and networking that NVIDIA’s hardware engineers design silicon on, spanning on-prem data centers and multi-cloud environments. You’ll operate as the peer counterpart to NVIDIA’s company-wide security organization and to hardware infrastructure engineering, translating enterprise security intent into controls that hold up at EDA scale without slowing chip design down.
Much of this is a build, not a maintain. You’ll have the authority to decide where standard tooling applies, where it actively cannot, and what NVIDIA engineers instead then lead a team to do it. If your depth is in large-scale networking and compute infrastructure at a hyperscaler, a security product company, or anywhere fleets and fabrics are the day job and you’ve carried real accountability for the security properties of those systems, you are exactly who we want to talk to. We don’t expect you to arrive fluent in every security product category; we do expect you to own security outcomes from day one and to acquire the remaining domain breadth fast. Strong infrastructure mastery plus sharp security instincts beats a broad product résumé here. This is a role for someone who believes security engineering is engineering: automation, instrumentation, and secure-by-default infrastructure not tickets, exceptions, and spreadsheets.
What You’ll Be Doing:
Build and lead the team. Grow and direct a team of engineers with a bias toward practical, production-proven results, and develop the leaders within it.  Own the technical roadmap. Partner with various other security teams and infrastructure engineering to architect the roadmap for EDA-specific security controls and ship them into production.
Make the network and platform your control plane. Protection doesn’t depend just on what’s running inside the node.
Engineer around hard constraints. Determine where conventional endpoint and workload security tooling fits, where it doesn’t, and design the alternative: security that protects multi-day compute jobs without degrading them.
Make enforcement uniform. Drive consistent application of security frameworks across on-prem data centers and multi-cloud platforms where “consistent” means enforced, not documented.
Run the full lifecycle of core infrastructure security technologies: selection, deployment, operation, and eventual replacement.
Automate the evidence. Build the KPIs, instrumentation, and audit workflows that make security posture across EDA systems continuously visible treating compliance evidence as an engineering output, not a manual exercise.
Think like an adversary. Mitigation planning across network, storage, and compute.
Champion security by design , embedding automation and secure defaults into the infrastructure lifecycle instead of bolting them on afterward.
What We Need To See:
12+ overall years building and operating production infrastructure at scale - network, compute clusters, and storage including 5+ years leading and managing engineering teams. A Bachelor’s degree in a relevant engineering field or equivalent experience.
Deep networking expertise applied to large compute environments.
Hands-on depth operating compute fleets at scale - provisioning, lifecycle, and the operational realities of long-running, high-value jobs.
Deep understanding of hyperscaler methodologies for operating large-scale systems with security and reliability as co-equal goals.
Experience securing performance-sensitive or high-throughput environments where standard agent-based tooling was constrained and you engineered a workable answer.
Extensive history of building and guiding engineering teams responsible for complex distributed or multi-cloud architectures.
Demonstrated ability to drive unified outcomes across organizational boundaries, with partners who do not report to you.
Exceptional communication skills credible with individual engineers and executive leadership in the same day.
Ways To Stand Out from the Crowd:
Built or operated infrastructure security capabilities at a hyperscaler or a security product company — you’ve engineered detection and enforcement systems, not just deployed someone else’s.
Experience with kernel- and fabric-level observability and enforcement - eBPF, in-line and out-of-band inspection, DPU/SmartNIC offload - as an alternative to heavyweight in-node agents.
Track record leading security or platform engineering inside EDA, HPC, or large research-cluster environments .   Breadth across security domains - IAM, EDR/XDR, CNAPP, CSPM, vulnerability lifecycle, zero-trust architectures - or a demonstrated pattern of picking up new domains fast.
Experience driving infrastructure-as-code and policy-as-code so secure configuration is the default state rather than an audited one, plus familiarity translating SOC2 / ISO27001 into real technical controls.

title: Senior Compute Platform Engineer, LSF - EDA Infrastructure
location: US, CA, Remote; US, TX, Austin; US, Remote
description:
NVIDIA's silicon does not tape out without the farm behind it. Our EDA compute environment runs millions of cores across federated LSF cells, and every simulation, synthesis run, and timing signoff on our roadmap passes through it. We are consolidating a dual-scheduler estate onto a single LSF platform, and we are looking for an engineer who knows LSF at the level of its internals — not just its configuration files.

Owning scheduler behavior across 15–25 federated LSF cells, including mbatchd and mbschd tuning, scheduling cycle analysis, and the contention patterns that appear as cells approach host-count ceilings.
Diagnosing MultiCluster forwarding problems — remote queue sizing, forwarding policy, cross-cluster pend behavior — where the symptom reported by users is "the farm is slow" rather than a clear failure.
Setting the technical design for cell topology and federation as the farm grows, and deciding what belongs in a cell versus what belongs in a new one.
Working with our IaC engineer to encode scheduler policy into a config schema that survives contact with MultiCluster, rather than one that looks clean and breaks at scale.
Partnering directly with CAD and methodology teams on workloads that break normal assumptions: 500GB+ memory jobs, interactive-versus-batch contention, and tape-out crunch bursts.

BS or MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or equivalent experience.
8+ years in HPC or large-scale batch compute, with 5+ years of that on IBM Spectrum LSF.
Demonstrated depth in LSF internals — you have debugged scheduler behavior beyond what the documentation covers, and you can explain a scheduling cycle from submission to dispatch.
Hands-on MultiCluster experience in a production, multi-site environment.
Strong Linux systems fundamentals, system programming languages and scripting in Python, Perl, and shell.

You have worked on LSF as a developer or in escalation engineering, rather than only as a consumer of it.
Experience with LSF integration points: esub, eexec, elim, submit wrappers, RTM, or the LSF APIs.

title: System Software Engineer, Performance - CUDA Driver
description:
The AI revolution is not powered by models alone, rather it advances when enormous amounts of computation become fast, efficient, and economical enough to turn new ideas into products people can use on a global scale. Faster training lets research and product teams test the next idea sooner. Lower-latency, higher-throughput inference makes AI assistants and agents more responsive and practical for more people. Shorter time to solution lets scientists and engineers explore more possibilities within the same time and energy budget.
At NVIDIA, performance is not a supporting metric — it is how architectural invention becomes useful computing. CUDA is a critical layer where that transformation happens, sitting beneath the frameworks, libraries, and applications used across AI, deep learning, and HPC, as well as graphics, automotive, robotics, and other CUDA-powered products. That gives this team unusual leverage: reduce overhead in a fundamental launch, synchronization, memory, or data-movement path—or create a new driver or runtime capability—and the improvement can flow through many downstream systems and be repeated across vast numbers of products. One well-designed systems feature can help customers obtain more useful work from GPUs already deployed while informing how future CUDA capabilities and GPU architectures are designed.
We are looking for systems software engineers who want to work at this leverage point. You will design and ship production C/C++ features and optimizations in the CUDA driver and runtime, trace important workloads across application, operating-system, CPU, interconnect, and GPU boundaries, bring up new platforms, and turn evidence into future software and hardware direction. Your work will not end at a benchmark: it can make AI tools more responsive and efficient, help scientists reach answers sooner, and enable intelligent machines and interactive products to operate within demanding real-time constraints. Over time, you can grow from owning critical features and performance paths to setting subsystem direction and leading hardware/software co-design across generations—helping build the computing foundation for the next decade of AI and accelerated computing.
What you'll be doing:
Design, implement, validate, and ship performance-centric features and programming-model capabilities in the CUDA driver and runtime, writing maintainable, well-tested production C/C++.
Optimize critical execution paths—including kernel launch, synchronization, memory management & movement, CPU–GPU coordination, and system interconnect use—for latency, throughput, bandwidth, efficiency, and scalability.
Own complex performance problems end-to-end - understand important workloads, form hypotheses, create focused measurements and models, isolate root causes across software and hardware boundaries, implement production solutions, and validate application-level impact.
Establish performance expectations for current and future platforms, characterize new silicon, close software and hardware gaps, and drive performance readiness through product release.
Translate workload and platform evidence into CUDA API and programming-model improvements, systems-software direction, and measurement-backed recommendations for future hardware architecture and implementation.
Partner with application, library, framework, operating-system, driver, runtime, firmware, GPU architecture, silicon, product, and customer-facing teams; communicate findings clearly and raise engineering quality through design and code reviews.
Lead complex feature development and cross-layer investigations across teams, define performance requirements and technical direction for major subsystems, mentor engineers, and shape hardware/software decisions for future product generations.
What we need to see:
A BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field—or equivalent practical experience — with at least 2 years of relevant systems-software development experience.
Strong production C/C++ systems-programming experience, including delivery of substantial features, optimizations, or production fixes in a complex codebase.
Strong operating systems and concurrency foundations, including threads, synchronization, processes, virtual memory, and user/kernel interactions.
Strong computer-architecture foundations, including processors, memory hierarchy, caching and coherence, data movement, and system interconnects.
Demonstrated success improving real software performance: measuring behavior, identifying the limiting mechanism, implementing an effective solution, and validating the result quantitatively.
Sound technical judgment, ownership of ambiguous problems, and clear communication across organizational and disciplinary boundaries.
Direct CUDA or GPU experience is valuable but is not required when accompanied by deep systems-software, operating-systems, computer-architecture, and performance-engineering foundations.
Ways to stand out from the crowd:
Experience developing GPU or accelerator drivers, runtimes, kernel software, firmware, compilers, or other performance-critical low-level systems.
Experience with pre-silicon analysis, platform bring-up, performance modeling, or hardware/software co-design.

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

We’re looking for an experienced Creative Director, Art to join our in-house creative team, focused on OpenAI’s business audiences. description:
About the Team
OpenAI’s Research Data team exists to accelerate the evaluation, safety and capabilities of our models and products. Made up of technical operators and software engineers, we design the methods through which we acquire and create data.

About the Role
As a Data Program Manager, Science, you will help researchers develop and execute scientific data programs, connecting OpenAI’s research priorities with relevant data, expertise and external partners.

You’ll work closely with researchers to understand their needs, assess the scientific and practical value of opportunities, and develop partnerships across the scientific ecosystem. The work could range from acquiring existing datasets to shaping research collaborations. You’ll carry opportunities from initial investigation through commercial discussions, agreements, delivery and research use, exercising sound judgement around sensitive data and relationships.

Our current work focuses particularly on biology and chemistry. We welcome different combinations of scientific, technical and partnership experience.

This role is based in our San Francisco HQ.

In this role, you will:

 - Develop data strategies with Research. Translate research goals, model limitations and evaluation gaps into evidence needs and success criteria. Compare acquisition with internal, public and commissioned alternatives.

 - Find distinctive sources for research. Build trusted local and international relationships across research and industry, including organisations at the scientific frontier.

 - Assess opportunities in scientific context. Inspect samples for provenance, context, quality and completeness. Assess usefulness, involving researchers and specialists as needed.

 - Shape partnerships with lasting scientific value. Understand partners’ ambitions and define pilots, deliverables and acceptance criteria, considering expertise, scientific contribution and continuing relationships alongside commercial terms.

 - Lead commercial and operational execution. Develop proposals, assess pricing and negotiate terms. Coordinate Legal, Privacy, Security, Procurement and engineering to clarify permissions, responsibilities and delivery.

 - Navigate sensitive collaborations. Understand institutional interests and confidentiality. Identify ethical, privacy, security and misuse concerns early, involving specialists to develop responsible arrangements.

 - Follow through into research use. Coordinate preparation, ingestion, access and documentation. Gather researcher feedback to inform whether to expand, change or stop.

 - Make thoughtful portfolio decisions. Recommend options based on research value, cost, timing and capacity. Identify shared needs and opportunities for useful collaboration across projects.

 - Make the work more repeatable. Use code, APIs, automation and AI tools to improve sourcing, assessment and delivery. Resolve recurring blockers with engineers and retain partner knowledge and research feedback.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have substantial grounding in biology, chemistry or related sciences through research, industry or equivalent experience, and engage critically with methods and evidence.

 - Have delivered complex scientific, data or partnership projects, with depth in one or more of scientific data and evaluation, commercial partnerships or research collaborations across organisations.

 - Exercise sound judgement: test claims, match evidence to research needs and make clear recommendations while acknowledging uncertainty.

 - Work directly with data: inspect unfamiliar files, investigate quality and use Python, SQL, APIs and AI-assisted coding to answer questions and reduce manual work.

 - Build trust through careful listening, precise questions and thoughtful negotiation. You bring relevant local and international relationships, or a demonstrated ability to develop them, and understand what partners value beyond the transaction.

 - Exercise discretion, recognising the limits of your expertise and authority and when scientific, ethical or safety questions need specialist input.

 - Thrive in a fast-moving environment, taking broad ownership across multiple projects and moving readily between scientific, technical and commercial questions. You prioritise thoughtfully as needs change, making clear decisions about where to focus and what can wait.

 - Enjoy getting your hands dirty, bringing energy and creative problem solving to unfamiliar or ambiguous opportunities. You turn them into practical plans and follow through on the details.

 - Learn exceptionally quickly, developing your understanding of AI training, evaluation and unfamiliar research areas to become a useful collaborator.

 - We welcome different combinations of scientific, technical and partnership experience. You do not need equal depth in every area.

description:
About this Team

The HR Business Partner (HRBP) team at OpenAI partners with leaders to navigate complex organizational and talent decisions where the right path is not always obvious. We are building a higher-leverage HRBP model: staying close enough to the business to understand its realities, while focusing our time on the work that requires judgment, influence, context, and leadership partnership.

This role is for an HRBP who can diagnose ambiguous situations, translate business strategy into organizational and talent decisions, coach leaders through consequential choices, and help build the operating rhythms that enable scale. While the role spans both strategic and operational work, the bar is not to be helpful on everything. The bar is to improve decision quality, strengthen leadership capability, and increase organizational effectiveness.

We operate with urgency, empathy, and sound judgment. We value sincerity, intellectual honesty, and collaboration over ego, and focus relentlessly on creating meaningful impact.



About this Role

This role is part of a shared hiring pathway for HRBPs at OpenAI. Instead of hiring directly for a single team, we evaluate candidates holistically first, then identify the best fit across our organization as you advance. This approach ensures alignment between your skills, interests, and where our needs are greatest—whether that’s partnering with technical leaders in engineering, supporting product teams driving user impact, or enabling operational excellence across business functions.

As a Senior HR Business Partner, you’ll be a trusted advisor to leaders and their teams. You’ll help set direction for how we organize, grow, and lead—stepping in as both a sounding board and a problem-solver. This role mixes strategic advising with hands-on support: you’ll design better systems, coach managers through complex situations, and help us make trade-offs that keep our people and mission in balance. This is an individual contributor role reporting to an HRBP Lead.



In this role, you will:

 - Shape high-performing, resilient teams: Partner with leaders to design structures, talent plans, and ways of working that enable strong performance and sustainable growth.

 - Collaborate for a seamless experience: Partner with fellow HRBPs, COEs, and cross-functional leaders to build an employee experience rooted in humanity, humility, and impact.

 - Evolve People programs: Strengthen performance, engagement, and retention processes—building solutions that are lightweight, scalable, and aligned with how OpenAI operates.

 - Guide and develop managers: Offer candid, actionable feedback and help managers build leadership muscle across their teams.

 - Anticipate and act fast: Stay close to the business to identify challenges early, diagnose root causes, and deliver lasting solutions that adapt as priorities shift.

 - Lead change that matters: Drive organizational changes with empathy, clarity, and rigor—finding creative paths forward when playbooks don’t exist.



You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - Deep HRBP expertise: 7–10+ years of HR experience, including at least 5 years as an HR Business Partner in high-growth or complex environments.

 - Strategic partnering: Able to see the big picture, guide leaders through tough trade-offs, and adapt quickly when priorities shift.

 - Multipliers who create impact: Skilled at giving candid feedback with care and building leadership capabilities across organizations.

 - Scrappy problem solving: Uses sound judgment to diagnose challenges, test creative solutions, and chart a path forward without a playbook.

 - Change leadership with calm & clarity: Brings steadiness, empathy, and influence in moments of ambiguity or transition.

 - High integrity: Known for discretion, fairness, and trustworthiness when the stakes are high.

This role is based in our San Francisco or New York office, and we aren’t considering remote applications at this time. We do encourage you to apply even if you prefer a fully remote role as location factors may change over time.

description:
About the Team

The OpenAI Risk & Audit team is building an enterprise risk capability for a company operating at the frontier of AI. We help leaders identify, understand, and manage the risks that matter most while enabling responsible innovation and durable growth.

We are developing a modern enterprise risk management (ERM) program and the technology foundation that powers it. Our work connects risk strategy, governance, compliance, and assurance with high-quality data, automated workflows, continuous monitoring, and AI-enabled analysis.

We partner across Finance, Security, Legal, Engineering, Product, People, Operations, and Internal Audit, and provide clear reporting to senior leadership and the Board. We aim to make risk ownership practical, decision-useful, and embedded in how OpenAI builds and scales.

About the Role

As the Head of Enterprise Risk Management, you will help build and lead an integrated ERM program and the ERM platform that supports it. You will establish common risk language, governance, and decision processes while translating them into scalable systems, data products, and workflows.

You will own enterprise risk assessments, maintain a centralized risk register, develop risk appetite and key risk indicators, and help leaders evaluate significant changes such as new products, markets, partnerships, major systems, and strategic investments.

This is a hands-on leadership role at the intersection of risk, operations, and technology. You will work with technical and business teams to connect source systems, improve data quality, automate evidence and control monitoring, and use AI to surface emerging risks and accelerate analysis.

You will also help create a strong risk culture, coordinate assurance across the three lines, and communicate complex issues with clarity and sound judgment. This is an opportunity to build a next-generation capability from the ground up.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and evolve OpenAI’s enterprise risk management framework, including risk taxonomy, governance standards, risk appetite, escalation thresholds, and mitigation expectations.

 - Lead enterprise risk assessments and maintain a centralized, decision-useful risk register that reflects strategic, financial, operational, technology, security, compliance, and emerging risks.

 - Establish key risk indicators, continuous-monitoring capabilities, and executive dashboards that translate complex data into clear signals, trends, and actions.

 - Enable risk-informed change governance for new products, markets, partnerships, acquisitions, major systems, and other high-impact initiatives.

 - Lead effective governance forums working cross-functionally with key partners such as Compliance, Finance, Security and others, and prepare concise reporting for senior leadership and the Board.

 - Define the strategy and roadmap for a modern ERM platform that will connect with systems across the enterprise including identity, finance, HR, ticketing, code, and others through reliable integrations and shared data models.

 - Coordinate risk activities across Finance, Security, Legal, Compliance, Engineering, Operations, and Internal Audit, clarifying ownership and reducing duplication across the three lines of defense.

 - Build, coach, and lead a high-performing team, strengthen first-line ownership, and foster a culture of practical risk management, curiosity, accountability, and continuous improvement.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - 12+ years of experience across enterprise or operational risk, compliance, internal audit, security governance, finance, or related fields, including significant experience leading ERM or GRC programs.

 - A track record of building or materially scaling an enterprise risk program in a fast-growing, technology-driven, or otherwise complex global organization.

 - Strong command of ERM and assurance practices, including risk appetite, risk assessments, KRIs, controls, issue management, and the three-lines model; familiarity with frameworks such as COSO or ISO/IEC 27001/27017/27018/27701/42001.

 - Experience advising executives and presenting risk information to senior governance bodies, with the judgment to make complex tradeoffs clear and actionable.

 - Technical fluency with GRC platforms, data architecture, APIs, system integrations, cloud environments, and automated workflows; experience with infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD, or policy-as-code is a plus.

 - Experience using data analytics, automation, or AI-enabled tools to improve risk sensing, evidence analysis, control monitoring, and reporting.

 - The ability to connect strategic, financial, operational, technology, security, and compliance risks and to work effectively across technical and non-technical teams.

 - Demonstrated success hiring, coaching, and developing multidisciplinary teams while operating effectively in ambiguity and at high velocity.

 - A relevant bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience; credentials such as CIA, CPA, CISA, CRMA, CRM, or an advanced business, legal, or technical degree are valued.

description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Growth team drives user and revenue growth across ChatGPT’s consumer and business segments and other OpenAI products worldwide. We work across the full funnel—from awareness and acquisition through activation, retention, and expansion—using experimentation, data science, machine learning, and product engineering to help more people discover and realize durable value from OpenAI’s products.

Our team partners closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Design, Finance, Lifecycle, and Growth Marketing. We move quickly, test rigorously, and hold a high bar for measurement, privacy, reliability, and user trust.




ABOUT THIS ROLE: 

We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to build the models and decision systems that optimize paid marketing investment for ChatGPT and other OpenAI products. You will develop budget allocation and control algorithms that determine where to invest, how quickly to spend, and how to adjust as performance changes.

The challenge is to make reliable decisions from noisy, delayed, and incomplete signals. You will combine machine learning, optimization, and experimentation to improve incremental growth and long-term user value within budget and efficiency constraints. You will own this work from problem formulation and prototyping through deployment, evaluation, and ongoing operation.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to eligible employees.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Build budget allocation algorithms. Decide how to distribute investment across channels, campaigns, and markets using estimates of marginal returns, while accounting for diminishing returns, uncertainty, and business constraints.

 - Develop spend pacing and adaptive control systems. Adjust budgets and spending rates as performance changes, balancing responsiveness with stability when feedback is delayed or noisy. Build in spend limits, monitoring, and safe fallback behavior.

 - Model marketing response and user value. Develop forecasts and models of conversion, long-term value, and saturation that help determine where the next dollar can have the greatest impact.

 - Evaluate decisions rigorously. Use simulations, backtesting, and online experiments to test allocation and control policies. Partner with Data Science to measure incrementality and validate whether offline improvements translate into better investment outcomes.

 - Own reliable production systems. Build data pipelines, training and inference workflows, and integrations that turn model outputs into budget decisions. Establish data-quality checks, monitoring, and retraining with thoughtful treatment of privacy and consent.

 - Turn business goals into optimization problems. Partner with Growth Marketing, Data Science, Engineering, and Finance to define objectives and constraints, communicate tradeoffs, and use evidence to improve investment decisions.

 - Help build a diverse and inclusive culture where people feel welcome, challenge assumptions, and collaborate with candor and respect.




You might thrive in this role if you:

 - 5+ years of experience as a Machine Learning Engineer, Applied Scientist, Data Scientist, or in a comparable quantitative engineering role, or an equivalent record of impact.

 - Experience building and operating production ML or quantitative decision systems, from problem formulation and data pipelines through deployment, experimentation, and monitoring.

 - Strong software engineering skills, proficiency in Python and SQL, and hands-on experience with ML frameworks and large-scale data systems.

 - Strong foundations in machine learning and statistics, with experience applying optimization or control methods to decisions under uncertainty.

 - Experience evaluating models or algorithms with noisy, delayed, or incomplete data, and the judgment to balance model quality, causal impact, and operational reliability.

 - The ability to turn ambiguous goals into focused experiments, interpret mixed results, and communicate clear decisions with technical and non-technical partners.

 - A collaborative working style and a commitment to deploying AI responsibly, in service of OpenAI’s mission to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity.

We combine machine learning and production engineering to make these capabilities accurate, efficient, and useful at scale, helping researchers assess changes and improve models and products.

We’re looking for a machine learning engineer to develop new classification and evaluation capabilities and bring them into production. This role combines traditional machine learning, model evaluation, and real-time engineering. You’ll own classifiers throughout their lifecycle, including supervised fine-tuning, distillation, evaluation, deployment, and production inference. You’ll work closely with researchers to identify valuable problems and with software engineers to make promising approaches useful at scale.

 - Experience reasoning about inference performance and the tradeoffs between quality, latency, and compute cost.

 - The ability to combine careful scientific judgment with a practical approach to shipping and operating software.

 - Comfort working closely with researchers and engineers on open-ended problems.

 - Fluency in using AI agents to move quickly across multiple workstreams in a fast-paced environment.

title: Procurement Coordinator
description:
About Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and advancing toward AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world environments. Working across the full model and systems stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the physical constraints of real-world systems to improve people’s lives.

About Role

We’re looking for a Procurement Coordinator to support the day-to-day purchasing and logistics needs of our Robotics organization. You’ll follow up on orders, coordinate domestic and international shipments, work with suppliers and logistics providers, and keep the details organized from purchase request through delivery.

This is an entry-level position for someone who is organized, curious, and eager to take ownership. You don’t need years of procurement experience, but you should be comfortable asking questions, learning quickly, and following through. When an email goes unanswered, you pick up the phone. When a delivery is at risk, you find out why, identify the next step, and keep the right people informed.

You’ll also help improve how we work. We expect you to adopt AI tools and build practical automations that reduce repetitive tasks, improve visibility, and make the supply chain team more effective. This role offers an opportunity to build a foundation in procurement, logistics, and hardware operations.



This role is based in San Francisco, CA and requires in-person presence 4 days a week and up to 10% travel to vendor sites.

In this role you will:

 - Follow up with internal teams to keep purchase requests and PO issuance moving on time, resolve missing information, and confirm that suppliers receive and acknowledge orders.

 - Track open orders through delivery, maintain accurate supplier commitments, and proactively follow up on lead times, shipment dates, and overdue items.

 - Coordinate domestic and international logistics, including scheduling couriers, arranging pickups, booking shipments, tracking deliveries, and resolving shipping exceptions.

 - Prepare and check commercial invoices, packing lists, and other shipping documentation. Work with suppliers, customs brokers, and internal specialists to address customs questions and support timely clearance.

 - Manage day-to-day coordination with third-party logistics providers (3PLs), including receiving, storage, outbound shipments, and resolving inventory or delivery discrepancies.

 - Keep purchasing and logistics records current, communicate clear status updates, and help resolve order discrepancies, returns, and missing delivery documentation.

 - Use AI, spreadsheets, and workflow automation tools to streamline order tracking, follow-up reminders, shipment updates, and routine reporting. Check that the resulting information is accurate and useful.

 - Support the broader supply chain team as priorities shift. Take action on open issues, call suppliers when email isn’t working, and escalate risks early with clear context and proposed next steps.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Are starting your career and want to build experience in procurement, logistics, or operations. Relevant experience can come from internships, school projects, part-time work, or other roles where you managed details and followed through.

 - Are highly organized and attentive to detail. You can keep track of multiple orders, deadlines, and follow-ups without losing sight of what matters most.

 - Have a bias for action. You’re comfortable contacting an unfamiliar supplier, asking direct questions, and following up persistently and professionally.

 - Communicate clearly and close the loop. People know what’s happening, what’s blocked, and what you’re doing next.

 - Are comfortable with spreadsheets and learning new systems. You actively experiment with AI tools and can turn a repetitive task into a more reliable workflow.

 - Adapt well to changing priorities, ask for help when needed, and exercise sound judgment about when to act independently and when to escalate.

 - Are curious about robotics, hardware, and how physical goods move through a supply chain. Prior exposure to purchasing systems, shipping, customs documentation, or warehouse operations is helpful but not required.

What success looks like:

Within the first 6 months, you will have:

 - Established reliable tracking for your assigned orders, with current commitments, clear next actions, and timely follow-up.

 - Built effective working relationships with suppliers, couriers, customs brokers, and 3PLs.

 - Become dependable at coordinating routine domestic and international shipments, preparing documentation, and escalating exceptions appropriately.

 - Earned the team’s trust through accurate records, responsive communication, and consistent follow-through.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Frontier Assurance team strengthens OpenAI’s safety decisions through independent expertise, rigorous assessment, and public transparency. We coordinate external evaluations of frontier models and safeguards, develop approaches such as embedded auditing, and manage the misalignment disclosure process and safeguard testing. Our work helps independent experts scrutinize OpenAI’s safety approach and ensures their findings inform consequential decisions about advanced AI systems.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a researcher on Frontier Assurance, you will build the technical foundations for rigorous assessments of frontier AI risks. You will help design technical assessments with external evaluators and internal teams: identify consequential safety claims to test, define the evidence and methods needed to assess them, and address gaps in coverage.

You will work closely with external evaluators and embedded auditors, helping them understand the systems they are assessing and access the models, data, and technical information their work requires. Where direct access is not possible, you will conduct experiments and analyses on their behalf, with methods and results they can meaningfully scrutinize.

This role combines research engineering, experimental design, and close technical collaboration. You will move between investigating specific safety questions, navigating complex internal systems, and building reusable tools that make assessments more thorough and efficient. Your work will help turn independent scrutiny into concrete evidence about model capabilities, safeguards, and remaining risks.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Help design assessments with external evaluators and internal teams: identify consequential safety claims to test, define the evidence and methods needed to assess them, and address gaps in coverage.

 - Support the technical execution of third-party assessments and embedded audits focused on frontier risks, working with evaluators to translate research questions into experiments, analyses, and evidence requirements.

 - Pair closely with external researchers to provide the data, technical documentation, and context needed to assess models and safeguards. Help them understand relevant system behavior, configurations, and limitations.

 - Design and implement secure access to assessment environments, working with research, engineering, and security teams to make relevant models, tools, and information available.

 - Conduct experiments and run analyses on evaluators’ behalf when direct access is constrained. Develop methods collaboratively, document implementation choices, and make results reproducible and open to challenge.

 - Build tooling that automates auditing, assessment workflows, and internal assurance work, including evidence collection, evaluation execution, and tracking changes across model or safeguard versions.

 - Reproduce external findings, investigate discrepancies with internal results, and work with relevant teams to test proposed mitigations and identify unresolved questions.

 - Document methods, findings, and limitations clearly so that evaluators and internal decision-makers can understand what the evidence establishes and where uncertainty remains.




YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have strong software engineering skills and experience building research tools, evaluation infrastructure, or systems for analyzing complex data.

 - Have practical experience working with modern machine learning systems, including designing experiments, running evaluations, and interpreting results.

 - Can navigate unfamiliar codebases and infrastructure, debug across system boundaries, and turn ambiguous research requests into reliable technical implementations.

 - Bring sound judgment to experimental design and measurement, including identifying confounders, limitations, and gaps in evidence.

 - Enjoy working closely with researchers, explaining technical systems, and helping others investigate difficult questions.

 - Value independent scrutiny and can support rigorous assessments that challenge internal assumptions.

 - Have an understanding of, or strong interest in, frontier AI risks, alignment, and the evaluation of safeguards.

title: SoC Engineer
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops custom silicon and systems for advanced AI workloads. Our first-party accelerator team works across chip architecture, design, software, and systems to build the computing platforms that power frontier models. We are a small, dynamic team that values technical breadth, hands-on engineering, and creative approaches to building complex hardware.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a SoC Engineer to help architect, design, and integrate OpenAI’s first-party AI accelerators. You will build the processor, interconnect, I/O, and platform infrastructure that connects our accelerator designs into complete, functional systems.

This role combines architectural judgment with hands-on implementation. You’ll work closely with design, architecture, verification, and software teams throughout development, from defining subsystem requirements and integrating IP to pre-silicon validation, silicon bring-up, and post-silicon debug. You should enjoy stretching across domains, rolling up your sleeves, and doing the work needed to make a complex system function end to end.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Define and implement SoC architectures spanning embedded processors, AMBA interconnects, peripheral subsystems, PCI Express, Ethernet and die-to-die interfaces.

 - Develop the microarchitecture and RTL design of subsystems supporting I/O and SoC functionality.

 - Integrate Arm Cortex-M and Cortex-A processors, AXI/APB fabrics, and third-party controller IP, including the RTL and glue logic needed to connect these components.

 - Develop reset and boot architectures, working with firmware and software teams to define sequencing, initialization, and survivability behavior.

 - Incorporate debug, test, and security requirements into the SoC architecture and implementation, partnering with other silicon designers to make the silicon observable, testable, and secure.

 - Drive PCIe and other I/O integration, including controller and PHY interfaces, high-speed SerDes, and die-to-die connectivity.

 - Contribute to power management and security architecture and design.

 - Work directly with third-party IP vendors to define technical requirements, evaluate IP capabilities, coordinate deliverables, and resolve issues from integration through silicon bring-up.

 - Work across architecture, design, verification, physical design, and software teams to define interfaces, resolve integration issues, and carry designs through pre-silicon validation and post-silicon bring-up.

 - Work closely with Firmware and Software teams to define boot, configuration and runtime behavior and functionality.

 - Build and apply automation and AI-assisted tools to accelerate design, IP integration, consistency checking, and debugging while maintaining engineering quality.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have experience in SoC architecture, RTL design, and subsystem or full-chip integration, with hands-on ownership through implementation and silicon bring-up.

 - Are familiar with Arm processor subsystems, including Cortex-M and Cortex-A, and AMBA protocols and interconnects such as AXI and APB.

 - Understand PCIe protocols and have experience configuring, integrating, and debugging controller IP.

 - Have experience integrating high-speed I/O, including SerDes/PHY interfaces and die-to-die links.

 - Have experience working directly with third-party IP vendors to evaluate technical fit, communicate requirements, and drive integration and debug issues to resolution.

 - Understand reset and boot architecture and the interactions between hardware, firmware, and software during initialization and recovery.

 - Have experience designing for debug, test, and security, and can reason about how these requirements affect the broader system.

 - Are comfortable writing and debugging Verilog/SystemVerilog and building scripts or tools to make integration work more efficient and reliable.

 - Enjoy stretching into multiple domains, learning unfamiliar parts of a system, and rolling up your sleeves to build and debug.

 - Enjoy working on a small, dynamic team where priorities evolve and engineers take broad ownership.

 - Are excited about creatively applying automation and AI tools to hardware design and integration work.

In this role, you will help government agencies, infrastructure owners and operators, and technology partners apply frontier AI to strengthen critical infrastructure security and resilience. title: Senior Quality Inspector (Electronics)
description:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots builds AI-native industrial robot arms deployed at manufacturing facilities across the U.S. In June 2026 we closed a $200M Series C at a $1B valuation, led by RoboStrategy with continued backing from General Catalyst and new participation from the Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund and Samsung Next.


About the role

Every robot we ship has to actually work — for years, in real factories, under real load. That comes down to what happens on the inspection bench before it ever leaves the building. As Senior Electronic Inspector, you're the final word on whether our PCBAs, cables, and harnesses meet the bar, and you're the person other inspectors turn to when the standard gets tricky.


What you'll do

- Inspect PCBA and electronic assemblies against IPC-A-610 acceptability criteria

- Inspect cables and wire harnesses against IPC/WHMA-A-620

- Lead First Article Inspections for electronic assemblies, setting the standard other inspections get measured against

- Mentor Receiving Inspectors on electronic inspection technique and how to actually apply IPC standards, not just cite them

- Own inspection records and traceability for everything electronic that comes across your bench

- Sit on the Material Review Board for electronic nonconformances and help drive real dispositions, not just paperwork

- Review electronic assembly drawings early and flag inspectability issues to NPI and Engineering before they become production problems

- Support 6S and FOD programs in the electronics QC area — FOD control especially, since a stray piece of debris in the wrong assembly is not a small mistake


What you'll bring

- 5+ years of electronic inspection experience in a manufacturing QC environment

- Current IPC-A-610 CIS or CIT certification

- Current IPC/WHMA-A-620 CIS or CIT certification

- Solid ESD knowledge and hands-on experience running or supporting an ESD program

- Ability to read schematics and electronic assembly drawings fluently, not just reference them


Nice to have

- Experience with industrial robotics control electronics, motor drives, or sensor systems

- Hands-on experience with microscopy and other visual inspection equipment


Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this role is $34-40/hour, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

Stripe’s Accounting Products team is building modern infrastructure for the Office of the CFO. Our vision is to give finance teams, and the agents that support them, one reconciled and explainable presentation of financial truth.
Today, the data and context required to make accounting decisions are fragmented across billing systems, contracts, spreadsheets, general ledgers, and the minds of the people doing the work. Finance teams spend significant time reconstructing what happened, determining the appropriate accounting treatment, reconciling results, and gathering evidence. Giving an agent access to the underlying data is not enough: it also needs the business context, accounting policies, approved judgments, and guardrails required to act reliably.
Revenue Recognition is our first major proof point. Stripe has a unique opportunity to help Billing and Metronome users turn complex revenue activity—including usage-based pricing, minimum commitments, credits, and contract modifications—into accurate, explainable journal entries. Our ambition is for agents to take on the investigation, configuration, and repetitive work while accountants retain control over consequential judgments and approvals.
Over time, we expect to expand into additional Office of the CFO workflows, and we are looking for a Staff Product Manager to help turn this vision into products that finance teams trust. This is a senior individual contributor role with significant ownership, autonomy, and influence across Product, Engineering, Design, Finance, Data Science, and Go-to-Market teams.

title: Hardware Engineer - Test Development

You will move between projects as needs shift, including next-generation vehicle platforms, production validation for our current robotaxi, and cold-weather qualification. Write test automation and tools in Python, and use AI tools to review specifications and test procedures, synthesize results and speed up test development.
